outline.heading: LABOR CODE
Chapter I
GENERAL PROVISIONS
Article 1. Scope of regulation
Article 2. Subjects of application
Employees, apprentices, trainees, and other workers without industrial relations
Employers
Foreign employees who work in Vietnam
Other agencies, organizations and individuals directly related to industrial relations
Article 3. Interpretation of terms
Employee means a person who works under a labor contract, is paid with wage and is managed, controlled and supervised by an employer

Employer means an enterprise, an agency, an organization, a cooperative, a household or an individual that hires or employs employees under labor contracts; if the employer is an individual, he/she must have full civil act capacity

Grassroots-level employees’ representative organization means an organization voluntarily established by employees working for an employer which protects employees’ rights and legitimate interests in industrial relations by collective bargaining or other forms prescribed by related law provisions on labor. Grassroots-level employees’ representative organization grassroots-level Trade Unions and employees' organizations at enterprises
Employers’ representative organization means a lawfully established organization which represents and protects the employers’ rights and legitimate interests in industrial relations

Industrial relation means a social relation arising from the hiring or employment and wage payment between an employee, an employer, their representative organizations and competent State agencies. Industrial relations are individual industrial relations and collective industrial relations
Worker without industrial relation means a person who does not work on the basis of a labor contract
Forced labor means the use of force or threat to use force or other tricks to force a person to work against his/her will

Labor discrimination means the discrimination, exclusion or prioritization on the basis of race, skin color, national origin or social strata, nationality, gender, age, pregnancy status, marital status, religion, belief, political belief, disabilities family responsibilities, or HIV infection, or for the reason of establishing, joining trade unions and participating in trade union activities, which impacts on equality of employment or career opportunities

Sexual harassment at the workplace means any sexual behavior of any person towards another person at the workplace without being desired or accepted by that person. Workplace is any place where the employee actually works as agreed upon or assigned by the employer
Article 4. State policies on labor

To guarantee the rights and legitimate interests of employees and workers without industrial relations; to encourage agreements providing employees with conditions more favorable than those provided by the labor law
To guarantee the rights and legitimate interests of employers, to ensure lawful, democratic, fair and civilized labor management, and to promote their social responsibility

To create favorable conditions for job creation, self-employment and vocational training and learning in order to acquire employment, and for labor-intensive production and business activities; to apply a number of provisions herein to workers without industrial relations

To adopt policies on the development and distribution of human resources; to improve labor productivity; to provide vocational training, training, retraining and improvement of occupational knowledge and skills for employees; to support job maintenance and change for employees; and to give preferences for employees with high professional and technical qualifications meeting the requirements of industrial revolution, national industrialization and modernization
To adopt policies on labor market development and diversify types of linkage between labor supply and demand
To encourage employees and employers to hold dialogues and collective bargains to establish harmonious, stable and progressive industrial relations
To ensure gender equality; to stipulate the labor regime and social policies to protect female employees as well as disabled, elderly and minor employees
Article 5. Rights and obligations of employees
An employee has the following rights

To work, freely choose a job, workplace or occupation, to participate in vocational training and to improve occupational skills; and suffer no discrimination, forced labor and sexual harassment at the workplace;

To receive a wage commensurate with his/her occupational knowledge and skills on the basis of an agreement reached with the employer; to receive labor protection and work in assured conditions of labor safety and labor hygiene; to take leaves according to the prescribed regime and annual paid-leaves, and enjoy collective welfare benefits;

To form, join and participate in activities of trade unions, occupational associations and other organizations in accordance with law; to request and participate in dialogues with the employer, implement democracy regulations, make collective bargains with the employer and be consulted at the workplace to protect his/her rights and legitimate interests; and to participate in management activities according to the employer’s regulations;
To refuse the employment which causes clear threats to his/her life and health during work performance;
To go on strike
Other rights according to law
An employee has the following obligations
To perform the labor contract, collective labor agreement and other cooperative agreements;
To obey labor discipline and internal working regulations; to follow lawful administration of the employer;
To implement the laws on labor, occupation, vocational training, social insurance, health insurance, unemployment insurance, labor safety and labor hygiene
Article 6. Rights and obligations of employers
An employer has the following rights
To recruit, arrange, manage, control and supervise employees; to perform commendation work and handle violations of labor discipline;
To form, join and operate in employers’ representative organizations, occupational associations and other organizations in accordance with law;

To request the employees’ representative organizations to have dialogue with the purpose of negotiating and signing a collective labor agreement; to participate in the resolution of labor disputes and strikes; to have dialogue and exchange opinions with employees’ representative organizations on issues related to industrial relations and improvement of the material and spiritual lives of employees;
To temporarily close the workplace
An employer has the following obligations
To perform the labor contracts, collective labor agreement and other lawful agreements; to respect the honor and dignity of employees;
To establish a mechanism for and hold dialogue with the employees and their representative organizations; to implement the regulations on grassroots-level democracy at the workplace;
To provide training, retraining and improvement of occupational knowledge and skills for employees serving the job maintenance and change for employees;

To implement other provisions of law on labor, occupation, vocational training, social insurance, health insurance, unemployment insurance, labor safety and labor hygiene; to elaborate and implement solutions for preventing and controlling sexual harassment at the workplace;
Article 7. Establishment of industrial relations

Industrial relations shall be established through dialogue, negotiation and agreement based on the principles of voluntariness, good faith, equality, cooperation and mutual respect for each other’s rights and legitimate interests

The employers, the employers’ representative organizations and the employees, the employees’ representative organizations shall establish progressive, harmonious and stable industrial relations with supports of competent State agencies

Trade unions shall, in collaboration with competent State agencies, facilitate the establishment of progressive, harmonious and stable industrial relations; supervise the implementation of the labor law; and protect the rights and legitimate interests of employees and employers

The Vietnam Chamber of Commerce and Industry, the Vietnam Cooperatives’ Union and other lawfully established employers' representative organizations shall act as representatives to protect employers’ rights and legitimate interests and participate in establishing progressive, harmonious and stable industrial relations
Article 8. Prohibited acts in the field of labor
Labor discrimination
Maltreating employees and forcing labor
Committing sexual harassment at the workplace
Making use of apprenticeship or on-the-job training for the purpose of self-seeking and exploiting labor or enticing or compelling apprentices or on-the-job trainees to carry out illegal activities

Using employees who have no vocational training or national occupational skills certificates for the occupations or jobs which require employees who have received vocational training or national occupational skills certificates

Enticing, promising or making false advertising or other tricks to deceive employees or to employ employees for trafficking in persons and forced labor, or making use of employment services or the sending of labor to work abroad under contracts to commit illegal acts
Illegally using minor employees
Chapter II EMPLOYMENT, RECRUITMENT AND LABOR MANAGEMENT
Article 9. Employment and creation of employment
Employment is any income-generating laboring activity that is not prohibited by law
The State, employers and the society have the responsibility to create employment and guarantee that all people with working ability have access to employment opportunities
Article 10. The right of employees to work
To freely choose a job, work for any employer in any location that is not prohibited by law
To directly contact an employer or through an employment service institution in order to find a job that meets his/her expectation, capacity, occupational qualification, and health
Article 11. Recruitment of employees
An employer has the right to recruit labor directly or through employment service institutions and labor leasing enterprises to recruit employees in accordance with the labor demand
Employees shall not pay fees for their recruitment
Article 12. Employers’ responsibilities for labor management
To make, update, manage and use labor management books in paper or electronic form and present them at the request of competent State agencies

To report on the employment of employees within 30 days from the date of operation commencement, to periodically report about labor changes in the course of operation to the specialized labor agencies of the provincial-level People's Committees and notify the social insurance agencies
The Government shall detail this Article
Chapter III
LABOR CONTRACT
Section 1
ENTRY INTO LABOR CONTRACTS
Article 13. Labor contract
Labor contract is an agreement between an employee and an employer on a paid job, wages, working conditions, and the rights and obligations of each party in industrial relations
Before accepting an employee, the employer and the employee shall enter into a labor contract
Article 14. Forms of labor contract
A labor contract must be established in writing and made in 02 copies, one to be kept by the employee and the other by the employer, unless otherwise stated in Clause 2 of this Article

The parties may enter into a verbal labor contract for jobs with a duration of under 01 month, unless otherwise stated in Clause 2 of Article 18, Point a, Clause 1 of Article 145 and Clause 1 of Article 162 herein
Article 15. Principles of entry into a labor contract
Voluntariness, fairness, good faith, cooperation and honesty
Freedom to enter into a labor contract which is not contrary to the law, the collective labor agreement and social morality
Article 16. Obligation to provide information before entering into a labor contract

An employer shall provide an employee with reliable information about the job, workplace, working conditions, working hours, rest time, occupational safety and hygiene, wage, forms of wage payment, social insurance, health insurance, unemployment insurance, regulations on business confidentiality, technological confidentiality, and other issues directly related to the entry into the labor contract as requested by the employee

The employee shall provide the employer with reliable information about his/her full name, age, gender, residence address, education level, occupational skills and qualification, certificate of health conditions and other issues directly related to the entry into a labor contract as requested by the employer
Article 17. Prohibited acts of employers when entering into and performing labor contracts
Keeping the employees’ original identity cards, diplomas and certificates
Requesting employees to make a deposit in cash or property as security for the performance of labor contracts
Forcing employees to perform labor contracts in order to pay debts to employers
Article 18. Competence to enter into labor contracts
Employees shall directly enter into labor contracts, unless otherwise specified in Clause 2 of this Article

For seasonal jobs or certain jobs with a definite term of less than 12 months, a group of employees who are full 18 years old or more shall authorize an employee in the group to enter into a labor contract; in this case, the labor contract must be established in writing and have the same effect as with each employee
The person entering into a labor contract on the employer's side is one of the following persons
The representative at law of the enterprise or the authorized person as prescribed by law;
The head of an agency or organization with legal status according as prescribed by law or the authorized person as prescribed by law;
The representative of a household, a cooperative group or other organizations without legal status or authorized persons as prescribed by law;
The individual directly using the employees
The person entering into a labor contract on the employee's side is one of the following persons
The employee who is full 18 years old or more;
The employee who is from 15 to under 18 years old with written consent of his/her representative at law;
The person who is under 15 and his/her legal representative;
The employee legally authorized to enter into a labor contract by employees in a group
Persons who are authorized to enter into labor contracts shall not authorize others to enter into the labor contracts
Article 19. Entry into more than one labor contract
An employee may enter into labor contracts with more than one employer, provided that he/she fully performs all the contents of the entered contracts

In case an employee enters into labor contracts with more than one employer, his/her participation in social insurance, health insurance and unemployment insurance shall comply with the laws on social insurance, health insurance, unemployment insurance, and labor safety and hygiene
Article 20. Types of labor contract
A labor contract must be entered into in one of the following types
An indefinite-term labor contract is a contract in which the two parties do not determine the duration and the time of termination of the contract;

A definite-term labor contract is a contract in which the two parties determine the duration and the time of termination of the contract within less than 36 months from the effective date of the contract
When a labor contract prescribed at Point b, Clause 1 of this Article expires and the employee continues working, it shall comply as follows

Within 30 days from the date of expiration of the contract, the two parties shall sign a new labor contract; pending the signing of a new labor contract, the rights, obligations and interests of both parties shall be performed in accordance with the contract already entered into;

If no new labor contract is entered into within 30 days from the date of expiration of the contract, the contract entered into under Point b, Clause 1 of this Article shall become an indefinite-term labor contract;

In case the two parties enter into a new labor contract with a definite term, only 01 additional definite-term labor contract may be signed; after that, if the employee continues working, an indefinite-term contract must be entered into, except for the labor contracts entered into by persons hired as directors of State-invested enterprises and other cases specified at Clause 1 of Article 149, Clause 2 of Article 151 and Clause 4 of Article 177 herein
Article 21. Contents of a labor contract
A labor contract must have the following principal contents
Name and address of the employer or full name, position of the person entering into a labor contract on the employer's side;
Full name, date of birth, gender, residence address, number of identity card or passport of the person entering into a labor contract on the employee's side;
Job and workplace;
Term of the labor contract;
Regimes for promotion and wage raise;
Working time, rest time;
Labor protection equipment for the employee;
Social insurance, health insurance and unemployment insurance;
Training, retraining and occupational skill improvement

When an employee performs a job which is directly related to business or technology secrets as prescribed by law, the employer shall reach a written agreement with the employee on the content and duration of protection of business or technology secrets, and benefits and compensation in case of violation

For employees working in agriculture, forestry, fishery or salt production, based on the type of job, both parties may skip some principal contents of the labor contract and reach additional agreements on settlement measures when the contract performance is affected by natural disaster, fire or weather
The Government shall stipulate the contents of a labor contract with an employee who is hired to work as director of a State-invested enterprise
The Minister of Labor, War Invalids and Social Affairs shall detail Clauses 1, 2 and 3 of this Article
Article 22. Annexes to a labor contract
An annex to a labor contract is a part of the labor contract and is as valid as the labor contract
An annex to a labor contract details, amends or supplements some provisions of the contract without changing the duration of the contract
Article 23. Effectiveness of a labor contract
Article 24. Probation
An employer and an employee may reach agreement on probation stated on a labor contract or enter into a probation contract
A probation contract must have the probation period and contents specified at Points a, b, c, dd, g and h, Clause 1 of Article 21 herein
Employees working under labor contracts with the duration of under 01 month are not subject to probation
Article 25. Probationary period
It does not exceed 180 days for the enterprise manager as prescribed by the Law on Enterprises, the Law on Management and use of state capital invested in business and production at the enterprise;
It does not exceed 60 days for posts which require professional and technical qualifications of collegial or higher level;
It does not exceed 30 days for posts which require professional and technical qualifications of intermediate level, or for technical workers and skilled employees;
It does not exceed 06 working days for other types of jobs
Article 26. Wage during the probationary period
Article 27. Expiry of the probation period
At the end of the probationary period, the employer must notify the probation result to the employee
During the probation period, each party may cancel the entered labor contract or the probation contract without prior notice and compensation
Section 2 PERFORMANCE OF LABOR CONTRACTS
Article 28. Performance of jobs under a labor contract
Article 29. Assignment of employees to perform jobs which are not stated in labor contracts

When meeting with sudden difficulties such as natural disaster, fire or epidemic, or taking measures to prevent and deal with a working accident, an occupational disease, an electricity or water supply incident, or when due to business and production needs, the employer may temporarily assign an employee to perform a job which is not stated in the labor contract provided that the assignment does not exceed 60 accumulated workdays within 01 year; the assignment exceeding 60 accumulated workdays within 01 year must be agreed by the employee

When an employer temporarily assigns an employee to perform the job which is not stated the labor contract as prescribed in Clause 1 of this Article, the employer shall inform the employee at least 03 working days in advance, clearly stating the duration of temporary job, and assign the job which must be suitable to the health and gender of the employee

The employee who performs a job which is not stated the labor contract is entitled to a wage for the new job. If the wage for the new job is lower than the previous wage, he/she is entitled to the previous wage for 30 working days. The wage for the new job must be at least 85% of the previous wage but not lower than the minimum wage

If an employee does not agree to temporarily perform a job which is not stated the labor contract for more than 60 accumulated workdays within 01 year and has to stop working, the employer must pay the wage in case of work suspension as prescribed in Article 99 herein
Article 30. Suspension of a labor contract
Cases of suspension of a labor contract
The employee is called up for military service or participates in the Militia and Self-Defense Force;
The employee is held in custody or detention in accordance with the criminal procedure law;
The employee is subject to a decision on application of the measure of consignment to a reformatory, compulsory drug detoxification center or compulsory education institution;
The female employee is pregnant in accordance with Article 138 herein;
The employee is authorized to exercise the rights and responsibilities of the ownership representative for the State capital portion at the enterprise;
The employee is authorized to exercise the rights and responsibilities of the enterprise for the enterprise’s capital invested in another enterprise;
Other cases as agreed by both parties

During the suspension of a labor contract, the employee is not entitled to the salary and the rights and interests already stated in the entered labor contract, unless otherwise agreed by the two parties or prescribed by law
Article 31. Reinstatement of employees upon expiry of the period of suspension of labor contracts
Article 32. Part-time employees
Part-time employee is a person who works for less than the normal daily or weekly or monthly working hours as provided by the labor law, the collective labor agreement or the employer’s regulations
An employee shall negotiate with the employer on working on a part-time basis when entering into a labor contract

Part-time employees are entitled to a wage and have the same rights and obligations as full-time employees and are entitled to equal opportunities and to non-discrimination and assured labor safety and hygiene
Article 33. Modification and supplementation of a labor contract

During the performance of a labor contract, any party that requests to modify or supplement the contents of the labor contract shall notify at least 03 working days in advance to the other party of the contents to be modified or supplemented
In case the two parties can reach an agreement, the modification or supplementation of the labor contract must be carried out by signing an annex to the labor contract or signing a new labor contract
In case the two parties cannot reach an agreement on the modification or supplementation of the labor contract, they shall continue performing the labor contract already entered into
Section 3
TERMINATION OF LABOR CONTRACTS
Article 34. Cases of termination of a labor contract
The labor contract expires, unless otherwise specified in Clause 4, Article 177 herein
The work stated in the labor contract has been completed
Both parties agree to terminate the labor contract

The employee is sentenced to imprisonment but is not entitled to a suspended sentence or does not fall into the case of being released as prescribed in Clause 5, Article 328 of the Criminal Procedure Code, or is sentenced to death or is prohibited from performing the job stated in the labor contract under a legally effective judgment or ruling of a court
The foreign employee working in Vietnam is expelled under the legally effective judgments or decisions of competent State agencies
The employee dies or is declared by a court to have lost civil act capacity, be missing or dead

The individual employer dies or is declared by a court to have lost civil act capacity, be missing or dead. The institutional employer terminates operation or declared by the business registration agency of the provincial-level People's Committee to have no representative at law or authorized person performing the rights and obligations of the representative at law
The employee is dismissed
The employee unilaterally terminates the labor contract under Article 35 herein
The employer unilaterally terminates the labor contract under Article 36 herein
The employer lays off the employee in accordance with Articles 42 and 43 herein
The labor permit of a foreigner employee working in Vietnam under Article 156 herein
The probation job is unsatisfactory to the probation agreement stated in the labor contract or one party cancels the probation agreement
Article 35. The right of employees to unilaterally terminate labor contracts
An employee may unilaterally terminate the labor contract and must notify the employer in advance
At least 45 days if working under an indefinite-term labor contract;
At least 30 days if working under a definite-term labor contract with a term of 12 months to 36 months;
At least 03 working days if working under a definite-term labor contracts with a term of less than 12 months;
For work-specific labor, the notification period shall comply with the Government's regulations
An employee may unilaterally terminate the labor contract without prior notice as follows
He/she is not assigned to the job or workplace or is not given the working conditions as agreed in the labor contract, unless otherwise specified in Article 29 herein;
He/she is not paid in full or on time as agreed in the labor contract, unless otherwise specified in Clause 4, Article 97 herein;
He/she is maltreated, beaten, verbally and physically humiliated with effects on his/her health, dignity and honor, or is subject to forced labor;
He/she is sexually harassed at the workplace;
He/she reaches retirement age as prescribed in Article 169 herein, unless otherwise agreed by the parties;
An employer provides unreliable information as prescribed in Clause 1, Article 16 herein, which affects the performance of the labor contract
Article 36. The right of employers to unilaterally terminate labor contracts
An employer may unilaterally terminate a labor contract in the following cases

The employee often fails to perform his/her job stated in the labor contract determined by the criteria to assess the job performance in the employer's regulations. The regulations on assessment of job performance shall be issued by the employer and must be revised by the grassroots-level employees’ representative organization if such organization exist;

The employee is sick or has an accident and remains unable to work after having received treatment for 12 consecutive months, in case he/she works under an indefinite-term labor contract, or for 06 consecutive months, in case he/she works under a definite-term labor contract with a term of from 12 to 36 months, or more than half the term of the labor contract, in case he/she works under a labor contract for a definite-term job or a specific job of under 12 months

If, as a result of natural disaster, fire, epidemic or enemy sabotage, or relocating and scaling down production and business at the request of competent State agencies, the employer, though having applied every remedial measure, has to cut jobs;
The employee is absent from the workplace after the time limit specified in Article 31 herein
The employee quits his/her job without plausible reasons for more than 05 consecutive working days;
The employee provides unreliable information under Clause 2, Article 16 herein when entering into labor contracts, thus affecting his/her recruitment
When unilaterally terminating a labor contract as prescribed at Points a, b, c, dd and g or Clause 1 of this Article, the employer shall notify the employee in advance
At least 45 days, for indefinite-term labor contracts;
At least 30 days, for definite-term labor contracts with a term of from 12 to 36 months;
At least 03 working days if working under a definite-term labor contracts with a term of less than 12 months and cases stipulated at Point b, Clause 1 of this Article;
For work-specific labor, the notification period shall comply with the Government's regulations
When unilaterally terminating a labor contract prescribed at Points d and e, Clause 1 of this Article, the employer shall not notify the employee in advance
Article 37. Cases in which an employer is prohibited from unilaterally terminating a labor contract

The employee is sick or has a work accident or occupational disease and is being treated or nursed under the decision of a competent health establishment, unless otherwise specified at Point b, Clause 1 of Article 36 herein
The employee is on annual leave, personal leave or any other types of leave permitted by the employer
The female employee is pregnant; the employee is on maternity leave or the employee is taking care of his/her small child who is under 12 months old
Article 38. Cancellation of unilateral termination of a labor contract
Article 39. Illegal unilateral termination of a labor contract
Article 40. Obligations of an employee when unilaterally terminating a labor contract illegally
Not to be entitled to a severance allowance

To compensate the employer half of a month’s wage in accordance with the labor contract and an amount equivalent to the wage in accordance with the labor contract for working days without prior notice
To reimburse training costs to the employer in accordance with Article 62 of this Code
Article 41. Obligations of an employer when unilaterally terminating a labor contract illegally

To reinstate the employee in accordance with the entered labor contract; to pay the wage, social insurance, health insurance and unemployment insurance premiums for the days during which the employee was not allowed to work, and an additional amount equal to at least 02 months’ wage in accordance with the labor contract

In case the employee does not wish to return to work, in addition to the compensation prescribed in Clause 1 of this Article, the employer shall pay a severance allowance in accordance with Article 46 herein in order to terminate the labor contract

In case the employer does not want to reinstate the employee and the employee agrees, in addition to the compensation prescribed in Clause 1 of this Article and the severance allowance prescribed in Article 46 herein, the two parties shall negotiate on an additional compensation which must be at least equal to 02 months’ wage in accordance with the labor contract in order to terminate the labor contract
Article 42. Obligations of an employer in case of changing structure, technology or economic reasons
The following cases are considered structural and technological change
Changing the organizational structure, reorganizing labor;
Changing the process, technology, machinery and equipment for production and business associated with the production and business lines of the employer;
Changing the product or product structure
The following cases are considered as economic reasons
Economic crisis or recession;
Implementing policies and laws of the State when restructuring the economy or implementing international commitments

In case there is a change in the structure or technology that affects the employment of many employees, the employer shall elaborate and implement a labor utilization plan in accordance with Article 44 herein; in case new jobs are created, priority must be given to re-training these employees for continued employment

In case more than one employee face the risk of unemployment or forced dismissal because of economic reasons, the employer shall elaborate and implement a labor utilization plan in accordance with Article 44 here in
In case the employer cannot employ and have to dismiss employees, the employer shall pay job-loss allowances to the employees in accordance with Article 47 herein

The dismissal of employees in accordance with this Article shall be implemented only after discussion with the grassroots-level employees’ representative organization of which the employees are members, and notification 30 days in advance to the provincial-level People’s Committee and the employees

Article 43. Obligations of an employer in case of split, separation, consolidation, merger; sale, lease, conversion of business type; transferring asset ownership or use rights of enterprises or cooperatives

In case of splitting, separating, consolidating, merging; selling, leasing, converting business type; transferring asset ownership or use rights of an enterprise an enterprise or a cooperative that effect the employment of many employees, the employer shall elaborate a labor utilization plan in accordance with Article 44 herein
The current employer and the succeeding employer are responsible for implementing the approved labor utilization plan
Employees who are dismissed shall receive job-loss allowances in accordance with Article 47 herein
Article 44. Labor utilization plan
A labor utilization plan must have the following principal contents
The lists and numbers of employees to be further employed, employees to be re-trained for continued employment and employees to be assigned part-time jobs;
The list and number of employees to be retired;
The lists and numbers of employees to terminate their labor contracts;
Rights and obligations of the employer, the employee and relevant parties in the implementation of the labor utilization plan;

When elaborating a labor utilization plan, the employer must discuss with the grassroots-level employees’ representative organization for the place where such organization exists. The labor utilization plan must be publicly notified to the employees within 15 days from the date of adoption
Article 45. Notice of termination of a labor contract

The employer must notify the employee in writing of the termination of the labor contract when it terminates as prescribed herein, unless otherwise specified in Clauses 4, 5, 6, 7 and 8, Article 34 herein
In case the institutional employer terminates its operation, the time of termination of the labor contract is the time of notification of operation termination
Article 46. Severance allowance

In case a labor contract terminates in accordance with Clauses 1, 2, 3, 4, 6, 7, 9 and 10 of Article 34 herein, the employer shall pay a severance allowance to the employee who has worked regularly for full 12 months or longer at the rate of half of a month’s wage for each working year, except for those eligible of pension in accordance with the law on social insurance and those specified at Point e of Clause 1, Article 36 herein

The working period used for the calculation of severance allowance is the total period during which the employee actually works for the employer minus the period during which the employee benefits from unemployment insurance in accordance with the law on social insurance, and the working period for which the employer has paid a severance allowance or job-loss allowance to the employee
The wage used for the calculation of severance allowance is the average wage in accordance with the labor contract for 6 consecutive months preceding the time the employee loses his/her job
The Government shall detail this Article
Article 47. Job-loss allowance

An employer shall pay a job-loss allowance to an employee who has worked regularly for the employer for 12 months or longer and loses his/her job under Clause 11 of Article 34 herein. The job-loss allowance is equal to 1 month’s wage for each working year but must not be lower than 2 months’ wage

The working period used for the calculation of job-loss allowance is the total time during which the employee actually works for the employer minus the time during which the employee benefits from unemployment insurance in accordance with the law on unemployment insurance and the working period for which the employer has paid a severance allowance or job-loss allowance to the employee
The wage used for the calculation of job-loss allowance is the average wage in accordance with the labor contract for 6 consecutive months preceding the time the employee loses his/her job
The Government shall detail this Article
Article 48. Responsibilities in case of terminating labor contracts

Within 14 working days after termination of a labor contract, the two parties shall make all payments related to the interests of each party; this time limit may be extended but must not exceed 30 days in the following cases
The institutional employer terminates its operation;
The employer changes the structure, technology or for economic reasons;
In case of splitting, separating, consolidating, merging; selling, leasing, converting business type; transferring asset ownership or use rights of an enterprise an enterprise or a cooperative;
In case of natural disaster, fire, enemy sabotage or epidemic

The payment of wages, social insurance, health insurance, unemployment insurance, severance allowances and other benefits of its employees according to the collective labor agreement and signed labor contracts shall be prioritized in case an enterprise or a cooperative has its operation terminated, is dissolved or goes bankrupt
The employer shall
Complete the confirmation procedure for payment time of social insurance and unemployment insurance and return it with other papers of the employee which are kept by the employer;
Provide copies of documents related to the working process of the employee if the employee so requests. The cost of copying and sending documents shall be paid by the employer
Section 4 INVALID LABOR CONTRACTS
Article 49. Invalid labor contracts
A labor contract is wholly invalid in one of the following cases
The whole contents of the labor contract are illegal;
The individual enters into the labor contract ultra vires or violate the principles of entry into labor contracts specified in Clause 1 of Article 15 herein;
The job agreed upon in the labor contract is prohibited by law
A labor contract is partially invalid when one of its contents is illegal but does not affect the remaining contents of the labor contract
Article 50. Competence to declare labor contract to be invalid
Article 51. Handling of invalid labor contracts
A labor contract which is declared to be partially invalid will be handled as follows

The rights, obligations and benefits of the parties must be settled according to the applicable collective labor agreements; in case the collective labor agreements do not exist, the provisions of laws prevail;
The two parties must modify and supplement the part of the labor contract which is declared invalid to conform with the collective labor agreement or the labor law

In case a labor contract is declared to be wholly invalid, the rights, obligations and benefits of the employee will be settled in accordance with law; in case it is signed ultra vires, the parties shall re-sign it
The Government shall detail this Article
Section 5 LABOR LEASE
Article 52. Labor lease

Labor lease means that an employee enters into a labor contract with an employer who is a labor leasing enterprise, after which the employee is transferred to work and managed by the other employer while still maintaining industrial relations with the leasing enterprise
Labor lease is a conditional business line performed by only enterprises licensed for labor lease and applicable only to certain jobs
Article 53. Principles of labor lease
The maximum duration of labor lease for employees is 12 months
The hiring party may use the leased employees in the following cases
Temporarily meeting a sudden increase in the labor demand in a given period;
Replacing employees during maternity leave, employees who have labor accidents, occupational disease or employees who are fulfilling citizen obligations;
There is a need to use employees with rich professional knowledge and high technical qualifications
The hiring party may not use the leased employees in the following cases
Replacing employees who are in the process of exercising the right to go on strikes or settling labor disputes;
There is no specific agreement on the labor leasing enterprise’s responsibility for compensation to the leased employees in case of labor accidents and occupational diseases;
Replacing employees who are fired due to changes in structure, technology, or economic reasons, or split, separation, consolidation or merger
The hiring party shall not assign the leased employees to another employer; not use the leased employees assigned by the unlicensed labor leasing enterprises
Article 54. Labor leasing enterprises
A labor leasing enterprise shall pay a deposit and obtain a license for labor lease
The Government shall provide the payment of deposits, the conditions and procedures for granting, regranting and extending licenses of labor lease, and the list of jobs allowed for labor lease
Article 55. Labor leasing contract
The labor leasing enterprise and the hiring party shall sign a written labor leasing contract, which is made in 2 copies, each to be kept by one party
A labor leasing contract must contain the following principal contents
Location of the workplace, working position for the leased employee, detailed description of the job and specific requirements for the leased employee;
Duration of the lease; the starting time of the lease;
Working time, rest time, occupational safety and hygiene conditions at the workplace;
Responsibility for compensation for labor accidents and occupational diseases;

The labor leasing contract must not contain any agreement on the rights and benefits of the employee that are less favorable than those agreed upon in the labor contract signed between the employee and the labor leasing enterprise
Article 56. Rights and obligations of a labor leasing enterprise
To ensure supply of a skilled employee who meets the requirements of the hiring party and the labor contract signed with the employee;
To inform the leased employee of the contents of the labor leasing contract;
To provide the hiring party with a brief personal record of the leased employee and his/her demands;
To ensure that the wage of the leased employee is not lower than that of a normal employee of the hiring party who has the same qualification and performs the same job or job of equal value;
To make a dossier stating the number of leased employees and the hiring party, and periodically report them to the specialized agency in charge of labor of the provincial-level People’s Committee;
To discipline leased employees violating labor discipline who are returned by the hiring party for their violations of labor discipline
Article 57. Rights and obligations of the hiring party
To inform and guide the leased employee to understand its internal working regulations and other regulations
Not to discriminate between the leased employee and its own employees regarding working conditions
To negotiate with the leased employee on working at night or overtime as prescribed herein

To negotiate with the leased employee and the labor leasing enterprise in order to officially employ this employee in case the labor contract between the leased employee and the labor leasing enterprise have not yet expired
To return to the labor leasing enterprise the leased employee who fails to meet the requirements as agreed or who violates labor discipline
To provide evidence of the leased employee’s violation of labor discipline for the labor leasing enterprise to consider and discipline such employee
Article 58. Rights and obligations of a leased employee
To perform the job under the labor contract signed with the labor leasing enterprise;
To comply with the labor discipline, internal labor regulations; the lawful management, control and supervision of the hiring party;
To be paid with a wage not lower than that of employees of the hiring party who have the same qualification and perform the same job or job of equal value;
To lodge a complaint with the labor leasing enterprise when the hiring party violates agreements in the labor leasing contract.;
To negotiate to terminate the labor contract with the labor leasing enterprise to sign a labor contract with the hiring party
Chapter IV VOCATIONAL EDUCATION AND TRAINING, AND OCCUPATIONAL SKILL IMPROVEMENT
Article 59. Vocational training and occupational skill improvement

An employee is entitled to freely choose vocational training, participate in assessment and recognition of national occupational skills, or develop occupational competency, which is appropriate to his/her employment demand and capability

The State shall encourage any eligible employer to carry out vocational training or occupational skill improvement for its current employees and other employees in the society through the activities as follows

Establishing a vocational training institution or opening vocational training classes at the workplace in order to train and retrain for improving occupational qualifications and skills for the employees; coordinating with vocational training institutions to open elementary, intermediate or collegial vocational training programs and other training programs in accordance with law;

Organizing occupational skill testing for employees; participating in an occupational skill council; forecasting the demand and elaborating occupational skill standards; organizing occupational skill assessment and recognition; developing occupational competency for employees
Article 60. Responsibilities of an employer for training, retraining and improving vocational qualifications and skills

An employer shall prepare annual training plans and budgets for training, retraining and improving vocational qualifications and skills for his/her current employees and training for employees before switching them to perform other jobs for the employer

An employer shall annually report on the results of training, retraining and improving vocational qualifications and skills to the specialized agency in charge of labor under the provincial-level People’s Committee
Article 61. Apprenticeship and on-the-job training to work for the employer

Apprenticeship to work for an employer is an employer's recruitment of an employee to conduct vocational training for him/her at the workplace. Duration of apprenticeship on the training program of each level shall comply with the Law on Vocational Education and Training

On-the-job training to work for an employer is an employer's recruitment of an employee to give job-practice and job-training in accordance with his/her recruited position at the workplace. Duration of on-the-job training shall not exceed 03 months

An employer that recruits apprentices or on-the-job trainees to work for him/her does not have to register such vocational training activity; may not collect tuition fees; and shall enter into a vocational training contract in accordance with the Law on Vocational Education and Training

An apprentice or on-the-job trainee must be full 14 years old or more and have appropriate health conditions required by the relevant apprenticeship and on-the-job training. The apprentices or on-the-job trainees of some occupations specified on the list of heavy, hazardous, dangerous occupations or extremely heavy, hazardous and dangerous occupations issued by the Minister of Labor, War Invalids and Social Affairs must be full 18 years old or more, except for those working in arts, physical training and sports

During the period of apprenticeship or on-the-job training, if the apprentice or the on-the-job trainee directly makes, or participates in the making of, products, he/she must be paid with a wage by the employer at a level agreed by the two parties
Upon the expiry of the apprenticeship or on-the-job training period, the two parties shall enter into a labor contract as conditions prescribed herein are met
Article 62. Vocational training contract between an employer and an employee, and job training expenses

The two parties shall enter into a vocational training contract in case the employee will be trained for vocational qualification and skill improvement or re-trained at home or abroad with the employer’s fund, including the fund donated by the employer’s partner
A vocational training contract must have the following principal contents
The trained occupation;
Training venue, training period and wages paid in the training period;
The period during which the employee commits to working for the employer after training;
Training expenses and responsibility to reimburse training expenses;
Responsibilities of the employee

Training expenses are those accompanied by valid documents on payment for trainers, training materials, training venues, machinery and equipment, practicing materials, support for trainees, wages, social insurance, health insurance and unemployment premiums paid for trainees during the training. In case an employee is sent to a foreign country for training, training expenses also include travel and living expenses during the period of training
Chapter V DIALOGUE AT WORKPLACE, COLLECTIVE BARGAINING, COLLECTIVE LABOR AGREEMENTS
Section 1 DIALOGUE AT WORKPLACE
Article 63. Conducting of dialogue at workplace

Dialogue at the workplace is the sharing of information, reference, discussion and exchange of opinions between employers and employees or their representative organizations on issues related to the rights, interests and concerns of the parties at the workplace to enhance understanding, cooperation, and make efforts towards solutions for mutual benefits
An employer shall conduct dialogue at the workplace
At least once a year;
At the request of one or both parties;
In the cases as prescribed in Point a of Clause 1, Article 36, Articles 42, 44, 93, 104, 118 and Clause 1 of Article 128 herein
Employers and employees or their representative organizations are encouraged to conduct dialogues in the cases other than prescribed in Clause 2 of this Article
The Government shall provide for the conducting of dialogue and implementation of grassroots-level democracy at the workplace
Article 64. Issues of dialogue at workplace
The issues of dialogue at workplace shall comply with Point c, Clause 2, Article 63 herein
In addition to the issues specified in Clause 1 of this Article, the parties may discuss one or several of the following issues in a dialogue
Production and business situation of the employer;
Performance of labor contracts, collective labor agreement, internal regulations and other commitments and agreements at workplace;
Working conditions;
Requests of individual employees and the employees’ representative organizations to the employer;
Other issues which concern one or both parties
Section 2 COLLECTIVE BARGAINING
Article 65. Collective bargaining
Article 66. Principles of collective bargaining
Article 67. Issues for collective bargaining
Wages, allowances, pay rise, bonuses, meals and other policies;
Workload and working time, rest time, overtime work, mid-shift breaks;
Ensuring employment for employees;
Ensuring occupational safety and hygiene; implementation of the internal working regulations;
Conditions and means of operation of the employees’ representative organization; relations between the employer and the employees’ representative organization;
Mechanisms and methods for preventing and settling labor disputes;
Ensuring gender equality, maternity protection, annual leaves; preventing violence and sexual harassment at the workplace;
Other issues that concern one or both parties
Article 68. The right to request collective bargaining of the grassroots-level employees’ representative organization at an enterprise

The grassroots-level employees’ representative organizations have the right to request collective bargaining when reaching the minimum number of members in the total number of employees of an enterprise as prescribed by the Government

In case an enterprise has many grassroots-level employees’ representative organizations meeting the provisions of Clause 1 of this Article, the organization has the right to request collective bargaining is the one with the largest number of members in the enterprise. Other grassroots-level employees’ representative organizations may participate in collective bargaining upon agreed by the employees’ representative organization having the right to request collective bargaining

In case an enterprise has many grassroots-level employees’ representative organization, but no organization meets the provisions of Clause 1 of this Article, the organizations shall voluntarily join together to request collective bargaining, but the total number of members of these organizations must reach the minimum rate as prescribed in Clause 1 of this Article
The Government shall provide for the settlement of disputes between the parties regarding the right to request collective bargaining
Article 69. Representatives for collective bargaining at an enterprise
The number of persons of each party to attend a bargaining meeting must be agreed by the two parties
The participants in the collective bargaining of each party are decided by that party

Each party is entitled to invite its superior representative organization to send participants acting as the representatives for collective bargaining and the other party must not refuse. The number of collective bargaining representatives of each party shall not exceed the amount specified in Clause 1 of this Article, unless otherwise agreed by the other party
Article 70. Process of collective bargaining

At the request for collective bargaining of an grassroots-level employees’ representative organization which is entitled to request collective bargaining according to Article 68 herein or at the request of the employer, the party receiving the request must not refuse the collective bargaining
The duration of collective bargaining shall not exceed 90 days from the commencement of the collective bargaining meeting, unless otherwise agreed by the parties

In the course of collective bargaining, at the request of the employee's representative party, within 10 days after receiving the request, the employer shall provide information on business, production and other issues directly related to the collective bargaining within the enterprise in order to create favorable conditions for collective bargaining, except for information on business secrets and technical secrets of the employer

The grassroots-level employees’ representative organization has the right to organize discussions and collect opinions of employees on the issues, methods of implementation and results of the collective bargaining

Collective bargaining meetings must be recorded in minutes which must specify issues that have been agreed upon by the two parties and issues on which opinions remain divergent. Minutes of collective bargaining meetings must be signed by representatives of the parties and the preparer of the minutes. The grassroots-level employees’ representative organization shall publicly announce the minutes of collective bargaining meeting to all the employees
Article 71. Failure of collective bargaining
Collective bargaining fails in one of the following cases
A party refuses to negotiate or does not conduct collective bargaining within the time limit specified in Clause 1, Article 70 herein;
The parties fail to reach an agreement after the time limit prescribed in Clause 2 Article 70 herein;
The time limit prescribed in Clause 2, Article 70 herein has not expired but the parties have mutually determined and declared that the collective bargaining has failed to reach an agreement

In case the negotiation fails, either party shall carry out the procedures for labor dispute settlement in accordance with this Code. When labor disputes are being settled, the employees’ representative organization must not organize a strike
Article 72. Sectoral collective bargaining and multi-enterprise collective bargaining
Principles and issues of sectoral collective bargaining and multi-enterprise collective bargaining shall comply with Articles 66 and 67 herein

The process of sectoral collective bargaining and multi-enterprise collective bargaining shall be decided by the parties, including the agreement to conduct collective bargaining via a collective bargaining council under Article 73 herein
The sectoral collective bargaining shall be decided by the sectoral trade union and the sectoral-level employees’ representative organization
Article 73. Multi-enterprise collective bargaining conducted by a collective bargaining council

Since consensus reached, the participating parties in multi-enterprise collective bargaining may request the provincial-level People's Committee of the locality where the participating enterprises are headquartered, or of the place chosen by the parties if the participating enterprises have their headquarters located in various provinces and municipalities, to set up a collective bargaining council to conduct collective bargaining

At the requests of the participating parties to multi-enterprise collective bargaining, the provincial-level People's Committee shall decide to set up a collective bargaining council to conduct collective bargaining. The members of such council are
Chairman of the Council, who is appointed by the parties and is responsible for coordinating the activities of the council and supporting the collective bargaining of the parties;
Representatives of the participating parties, who are appointed by each party; the number of the representatives in the council shall be agreed by the parties;
Representatives of provincial-level People's Committees
The collective bargaining council conducts bargaining at the request of the parties and terminates its operation when a multi-enterprise collective labor agreement is reached by the parties
The Minister of Labor, War Invalids and Social Affairs shall define the functions, tasks and activities of collective bargaining councils
Article 74. Responsibilities of the provincial-level People's Committee in collective bargaining
To organize training and retraining in collective bargaining skills for participating parties
To elaborate and provide information and data related to socio-economic issues, labor markets and industrial relations to support and promote collective bargaining

To assist the collective bargaining parties to reach an agreement in the process of collective bargaining proactively or at request of both parties; in case of no request, the active support of the provincial-level People's Committee shall only be given if the parties agree
To set up a collective bargaining council at the request of multi-enterprise collective bargaining parties as prescribed in Article 73 herein
Section 3.
COLLECTIVE LABOR AGREEMENTS
Article 75. Collective labor agreements
Collective labor agreement is a written agreement reached through collective bargaining and signed by the parties
The contents of a collective labor agreement must not be against the labor law and must be more favorable for the employees than what is provided by law
Article 76. Collecting comments and signing of a collective labor agreement

With regard to the enterprise collective labor agreement, the draft collective labor agreement negotiated by the parties must be consulted by all employees in the enterprise before signing. An enterprise collective labor agreement shall only be signed when there are more than 50% of the employees of the enterprise voted for voting agree

In the case of collective bargaining agreements, the branches and subjects to collect opinions include all members of the management board of the representative organizations of workers at the enterprises participating in the negotiation. The sector collective labor agreement can only be signed when there are more than 50% of the total number of people voted for voting agree

Time, place and method of collecting voting ideas on the draft collective labor agreement shall be decided by the workers' representative organization but must not affect the production and business activities of organizations in negotiation. The employer must not cause difficulties, obstruct or interfere with the process of organizing representatives of employees to vote on the draft agreement
The collective labor agreement is signed by the legal representative of the negotiating parties

Collective labor agreements must be sent to each contracting party and to the labor specialized agencies of the provincial-level People's Committees according to the provisions of Article 77 of this Code
After the collective labor agreement is signed, the employer must disclose to his employees
The Government shall detail this Article
Article 77. Sending of the collective labor agreement
Article 78. Validity and duration of collective labor agreements

The effective date of the collective labor agreement is agreed upon by the parties and stated in the agreement. In case the parties do not agree on the effective date, the collective labor agreement takes effect from the signing date

The enterprise collective labor agreement takes effect on the employer and all employees of the enterprise. The sector collective labor agreement and the collective labor agreement with many enterprises shall be valid for all employers and employees of enterprises participating in the collective labor agreement

The collective labor agreement has a term of between 01 year and 03 years. The specific period of time shall be agreed upon by the parties and stated in the collective labor agreement. The parties shall have the right to agree on different terms for the contents of a collective labor agreement
Article 79. Implementation of collective labor agreements at enterprises
Employers and employees, including employees who come to work after the effective date of a collective labor agreement, shall be obliged to fully implement the effective collective labor agreement

Where the rights, obligations, and interests of the parties to a labor contract concluded before the effective date of the collective labor agreement are lower than the relevant provisions of the collective labor agreement then provisions of the collective labor agreement shall prevail. The employer's regulations which are not in accordance with the collective labor agreement must be amended accordingly. In the time of the amendment, the relevant content of the collective labor agreement shall apply

When one party considers that the other party has not fully implemented or violated the collective labor agreement, such party shall have the right to request the proper implementation of the collective labor agreement and the parties are responsible for considering and settling. If it is not resolved, each party shall have the right to request the settlement of collective labor disputes in accordance with the law

Article 80. Implementation of enterprise collective labor agreements in case of division, separation, consolidation or merger; sale, lease, conversion of business type; transfer of ownership, right to use assets of the enterprise

In cases of division, splitting, consolidation or merger; sale, lease, conversion of business type; transfer of the ownership or right to use the property of the enterprise, the next employer and the representative organization of the employee have the right to negotiate in accordance with Article 68 of this Code based on the utilization plan, with regard to considering the option of continuing to implement, amend and supplement the old enterprise collective labor agreement or negotiate to sign a new collective labor agreement

In case the enterprise collective labor agreement ceases to be effective due to the termination of operation by the employer, the employee's interests shall be settled according to the provisions of law
Article 81. Relationship between enterprise collective labor agreements, sectoral-level collective bargaining agreements, and collective enterprise agreements

In cases where an enterprise collective labor agreement or a collective labor agreement contains multiple enterprises and a collective labor agreement stipulating different rights, obligations, and interests of employees, it must be implemented according to the content that is most beneficial to the employees

Enterprises subject to the application of a sectoral collective labor agreement or a collective labor agreement with multiple enterprises but have not yet had a collective labor agreement may formulate a collective labor agreement businesses with content that are more beneficial to workers than industry collective bargaining agreements or collective labor agreements with many businesses

To encourage enterprises that have not yet elaborated the sectoral collective bargaining agreement or the collective bargaining agreement to have more enterprises implementing content that is more beneficial to employees of the sectoral collective labor agreement or labor agreement collective action that has multiple businesses
Article 82. Amendments and supplements to collective labor agreements
Collective labor agreements may be amended and supplemented only by voluntary agreements of the parties through collective bargaining

When the provisions of law change resulting in a collective labor agreement that is no longer in accordance with the provisions of law, the parties must proceed to amend and supplement the collective labor agreement to suit provisions of law. During the period of amendment and supplementation of the collective labor agreement, the rights of the employee shall be implemented in accordance with the law
Article 83. Collective labor agreement expires
Article 84. Extending the scope of application of a sector collective labor agreement or a collective labor agreement with many enterprises

When a sectoral collective bargaining agreement or collective bargaining agreement has many enterprises, the scope of application shall account for over 75% of the employees or over 75% of enterprises of the same industry, line or field in the industrial park, an economic zone, an export processing zone, or a high-tech park, the employer or its representative organization shall request the competent state agency to decide to expand the scope of partial application or the entire agreement with enterprises of the same industry, industry, and sector in industrial parks, economic zones, export processing zones, and hi-tech parks

The Government shall detail Clause 1 of this Article; stipulate the order, procedures, and competence to decide to expand the scope of application of a collective labor agreement prescribed in Clause 1 of this Article
Article 85. Joining and withdrawing from a sector collective labor agreement or collective labor agreement with many enterprises

An enterprise may join a sectoral collective labor agreement, a collective labor agreement with many enterprises with the consent of all employers and the representative organization of employees at the enterprise which is a member of the agreement, except for the case specified in Clause 1, Article 84 of this Code

A member enterprise of a sectoral collective labor agreement having multiple businesses can withdraw from the collective labor agreement when having the consent of all employers and organizations, representatives of employees at the enterprise are members of the agreement, except for cases of special difficulties in production and business activities
The Government shall detail this Article
Article 86. Invalid collective labor agreement
Collective labor agreement is partially invalid when one or some of the contents of the collective labor agreement violates the law
The collective labor agreement is totally invalidated in one of the following cases
All contents of the collective labor agreement violate the law;
The signer is not under the authority;
Failure to comply with the process of negotiation and signing of the collective labor agreement
Article 87. Competence to declare a collective bargaining agreement is invalid
Article 88. Handling of invalid collective labor agreements
Article 89. Expenses for negotiating and signing collective labor agreements
Chapter VI
WAGE
Article 90. Wages
Wage means the amount of money the employer pays to the employee under an agreement to perform the job, including the wage based on the job or title, wage allowance and other additional payments
The wage according to the job or title cannot be lower than the minimum wage
Employers must ensure equal pay, regardless of gender, for employees of equal value
Article 91. Minimum wage

The minimum wage is the lowest wage paid to employees who perform the simplest jobs under normal working conditions in order to ensure the minimum living standards of employees and their families, in accordance with social and economic development conditions
The minimum wage is set by region, decided by month and hour

The minimum wage is adjusted based on the minimum living standard of workers and their families; the correlation between the minimum wage and the market wage; consumer price index, economic growth rate; labor supply and demand relations; employment and unemployment; labor productivity; affordability of the business
The Government shall detail this Article; decide and publish the minimum wage based on recommendations of the National Wage Council
Article 92. National Wages Council
The National Wage Council is an agency that advises the Government on minimum wages and wage policies for employees

The Prime Minister shall set up a National Wages Council comprising members who are representatives of the Ministry of Labor, War Invalids and Social Affairs, the Vietnam General Confederation of Labor, a number of user representative organizations for central workers and independent experts
The Government shall specify the functions, tasks, organizational structure and operation of the National Wage Council
Article 93. Formulation of wage scales, payroll and labor norms

The employer must establish a wage scale, payroll, and labor norms as a basis for recruiting and employing employees, agree upon a wage according to the job or title stated in the labor contract and pay wage for employees
The labor level must be the average to ensure that a majority of workers can perform the job without having to extend normal working hours and must finish before official issuance

The employer must consult the representative organization of the employee at the grassroots level for the place where the labor representative organization at the grassroots level is formulated when setting the wage scale, payroll, and labor norms
Article 94. Wage payment principles
The employer must pay employees directly, fully and on time. In case the employee cannot receive wage directly, the employer may pay the wage to the one the employee legally authorizes

The employer must not restrict or interfere with the employee's right to self-determination of wage payment. It is forbidden to force employees to spend wages on the purchase of goods or services of the employer or other units designated by the employer
Article 95. Wage payment
Employers pay employees based on agreed wages, labor productivity and quality of job performance
Wages stated in labor contracts and wages paid to employees in Vietnam dong, in case foreign employees in Vietnam may be in foreign currencies
Each time of payment, the employer must notify the payroll list to the employee, clearly stating his/her wage, overtime pay, night work wage, content and amount deducted (if any)
Article 96. Forms of payment
The employer and the employee agree on the method of payment based on time, product or package
Wages are paid in cash or through the employees' personal accounts opened at banks
The Government shall detail this Article
Article 97. Term of wage payment

Employees entitled to hourly, daily or weekly wages shall be paid after the working hours, days, weeks or gross payment shall be agreed upon by the two parties but must not be paid in a lump sum for more than 15 days
The employee who receives a monthly wage is paid once a month or once every half a month. The time of payment is agreed upon by the two parties and must be set at a cyclical time

Employees enjoying wages according to product or piece rate shall be paid according to the agreement of the two parties. If the job has to be worked for many months, the monthly wage will be advanced according to the amount of work done in the month

Where due to force majeure reasons, the employer has sought all remedies but cannot pay the wage on time, it must not be later than 30 days. If the employer pays a late wage of 15 days or more, the employer must compensate the employee for an amount of at least equal to the interest of the deferred payment calculated according to the one-month deposit interest rate due to the bank where the employer opens the payroll account for the employee announced at the time of pay
Article 98. Wage for overtime pay work and night work
An employee who performs overtime work must be paid according to the wage unit or wage for his/her current job as follows
On normal days, at least equal to 150%;
On weekends, at least equal to 200%;

On public holidays, Lunar New Year Holidays and paid leave days, at least equal to 300%, excluding the wage for public holidays, Lunar New Year Holidays and paid leave days of employees who receive daily wages

An employee who performs night work must be paid with an additional amount at least equal to 30% of the wage calculated according to the wage unit or the wage for a job performed during normal workdays

An employee who performs overtime work at night must be paid under Clauses 1 and 2 of this Article. He/she must be paid with an additional amount equal to 20% of the wage calculated according to the wage unit or the wage for a job performed during daytime of normal workdays, weekends or public holidays, Lunar New Year Holidays
The Government shall detail this Article
Article 99. Wage in case of work suspension
If due to the fault of the employer, the employee shall be entitled to payment of the full wage according to the labor contract;

If due to his/her fault, he/she shall not be entitled to payment of wage; other employees in the same unit who also have to suspend the work shall be entitled to the wages as agreed upon by the two parties, provided that those wages are not lower than the regional minimum wage;

If due to power or water incidents rather than the fault of the employer, employees or for other objective reasons such as natural calamity, fire, dangerous epidemic, enemy sabotage, relocation of the operation place upon request of a competent state agency, or for economic reasons, the wage for work suspension must be agreed by the two parties as follows
In case of work suspension for 14 working days or less, the wage for work suspension shall be agreed by the two parties but shall not be lower than the minimum wage;

In case of work suspension for more than 14 working days, the wage for work suspension shall be agreed by the two parties but shall ensure that the wage in the first 14 days is not lower than the minimum wage
Article 100. Payment of wage via foreman

In case foremen or similar intermediary persons are used, the employer who is the principal owner shall have a list and addresses of these people together with a list of employees working with them, and shall ensure that they comply with the law on wage payment and occupational safety and hygiene

In case a foreman or similar intermediary person fails to pay wages or pays insufficient wages and fails to ensure other interests of employees, the employer who is the principal owner shall pay wages to, and to ensure such interests of, the employees
Article 101. Advance of wage
An employee shall be given a wage in advance according to the conditions agreed upon by the two parties

An employer shall advance a wage amount to an employee corresponding to the number of days off which the employee takes to perform citizens’ obligations from 01 week to 01 month at most according to the labor contract and the employee shall refund this advance amount
When taking annual leave, an employee is entitled to an advance payment of at least equal to the wage of days off
Article 102. Deduction of wages
An employer may only make deductions from the wage of an employee for compensation for damage of the employer’s tools, equipment and assets in accordance with Article 129 of this Code
The employee shall be entitled to know the reasons for his/her wage deductions
A monthly wage deduction must not exceed 30% of the monthly wage of an employee after having paid compulsory social insurance, health insurance and unemployment and personal income tax
Article 103. Wage raise, rank promotion, allowances and subsidies
Article 104. Bonuses
Bonus is a sum of money or property or other forms that an employer rewards his/her employees on the basis of annual business results and the level of work performance of employees

Bonus regulations shall be decided and publicly announced by the employer at the workplace after consultation with the representative organization of the grassroots-level employees in the case there is a representative organization of the grassroots-level employees
Chapter VII
WORKING TIME AND REST TIME
Section 1
WORKING TIME
Article 105. Normal working time
Normal working time shall not exceed 8 hours per day or 48 hours per week

An employer may determine the working time on an hourly, daily or weekly basis but must notify his/her employees; in case of working on a weekly basis, the normal working time shall not exceed 10 hours per day and not exceed 48 hours per week
An employer shall ensure the working time limit for employees who are exposed to dangerous and harmful factors in accordance with national technical regulations and relevant laws
Article 106. Working hours at night
Article 107. Overtime work
Overtime is time worked in addition to normal working hours prescribed in the law, collective labor agreements or internal working regulations
An employer may request an employee to work overtime upon fully meeting the following conditions
Obtaining the employee’s consent;

Ensuring that the number of overtime working hours of the employee does not exceed 50% of the normal working hours per day; in case of applying regulations on weekly work, the total of normal working hours and overtime working hours must not exceed 12 hours per day; does not exceed 40 hours per month;
Ensuring that the number of overtime working hours of the employee does not exceed 200 hours per year, except for the case specified in Clause 3 of this Article
An employer may request an employee to work overtime for no more than 300 hours per year in the following industries, jobs or cases
