Producing, processing and exporting textile, garment, leather, shoes, electric and electronic products; processing agricultural, forestry, salt-producing and aquatic products;
Producing, supplying electricity, telecommunications, oil refining; water supply and drainage;
In case of handling jobs requiring employees with high professional and technical qualifications which labor market can not provide sufficient and timely;

In case of urgent work that cannot be delayed, due to the seasonality and timing of raw materials, products or to solve jobs arising due to unpredictable objective factors result from weather consequences, natural disasters, enemy sabotage, fire, lack of electricity, lack of raw materials and technical problems of production lines;
If an employer organizes the overtime working as prescribed in Clause 3 of this Article, he/she shall send a written notification to the labor agency of the provincial People's Committee
The Government shall detail this Article
Article 108. Working overtime in special cases
Implementing a call-up or mobilization in order to ensure national defense or security as prescribed by law;

Implementing the tasks to protect human lives and assets of agencies, organizations or individuals in the prevention and remediation of consequences of a natural calamity, fire, dangerous epidemic or disaster, except for the case that may affect the employee’s health and lives in accordance with the law on occupational safety and hygiene
Section 2
REST TIME
Article 109. Rest breaks during working hours

An employee who works for more than 06 hours per day under Article 105 of this Code shall be entitled to a break of at least 30 minutes in the middle of working. If working at night, he/she shall be entitled to a break of at least 45 minutes in the middle of working
Besides the breaks in the middle of working prescribed in Clauses 1 of this Article, the employer shall determine other short breaks and include them in the internal working regulations
Article 110. Breaks between shifts
Article 111. Weekly breaks

Every week, an employee shall be entitled to a break of at least 24 consecutive hours. In case it is impossible for an employee to have a weekly break due to the cycle of work, the employer shall ensure the employee have at least 4 days off on average in a month
An employer may determine and schedule weekly breaks either on Sunday or another fixed weekday but shall include them in the internal working regulations
In case weekly days off coincide with public holidays and New Year holidays specified in Clause 1, Article 112 of this Code, employees shall be entitled to a weekly day off on the next working day
Article 112. Public and New Year holidays
Employees are entitled to a leave of absence from work and full pay during the following holidays
Calendar New Year Holiday

outline.heading: Lunar New Year Holidays
Liberation Day
International Labor Day
outline.body: 01 day (the first day of May of each calendar year);

outline.heading: Commemorative Celebration of Vietnam’s Forefather - Kings Hung
outline.body: 01 day (the tenth of March of the lunar year).

outline.heading: An foreign employee working in Vietnam, in addition to the public holidays specified in Clause 1 of this Article, he/she shall be entitled to 01 traditional new year holiday and 01 national day of his/her country
Annually, on the basis of practical conditions, the Prime Minister shall decide on specific holidays prescribed at Points b and dd, Clause 1 of this Article
Article 113. Annual leave
An employee who has been working for an employer for full 12 months shall be entitled a fully paid annual leave as stated in his/her labor contract as follows
12 working days for an employee working in normal conditions;
14 working days for a juvenile employee, a disabled employee or an employee doing a heavy, hazardous and dangerous job;
16 working days for an employee doing an extremely heavy, hazardous or dangerous job
An employee who has been working less than 12 months for an employer shall be entitled to take annual leave with the number of leave days proportionate to the working time
An employee who, due to job leaving or job loss, fails to take or fully take his/her annual leave shall be entitled to a cash payment for the untaken leave days

An employer shall be responsible for setting the annual leave schedule after consulting with employees and must notify it in advance to them. An employee may reach an agreement with the employer on taking annual leave in installments or combining annual leaves of maximum every three years
When taking annual leave before the period of payment, an employee shall be entitled to an advance payment in accordance with Clause 3, Article 101 of this Code

When taking annual leave, if an employee travels by road, railway or waterway and the return trip takes more than 02 days, the travel days from the 3rd day onward will be added to the annual leave and this will be applied for only one annual leave in a year
The Government shall detail this article
Article 114. Annual leave increased based on the length of employment
Article 115. Personal leave and unpaid leave
An employee may take fully paid leave for personal reasons and must notify the employer in the following cases
Marriage
Marriage of his/her child
Death of a blood parent, an adoptive parent, a blood parent of his/her spouse, an adoptive parent of his/her spouse, his/her spouse or child

An employee may take a day off without pay and shall inform the employer when a paternal or maternal grandparent or blood sibling dies; his/her father or mother gets married; or a blood sibling gets married
An employee may agree with the employer on unpaid leave in addition to the leaves specified in Clauses 1 and 2 of this Article
Section 3
WORKING TIME AND REST TIME FOR PEOPLE DOING SPECIAL JOBS
Article 116. Working time, rest time for persons doing special jobs
Chapter VIII
LABOR DISCIPLINE AND MATERIAL RESPONSIBILITIES
Section 1
LABOR DISCIPLINE
Article 117. Labor discipline
Article 118. Internal working regulations
An employer employing 10 or more employees must have internal working regulations in writing
The contents of internal working regulations must not be contrary to the labor law and other relevant laws. The internal working regulations contain the following principal contents
Working time and rest time;
Order at workplace;
Occupational safety and hygiene at workplace;
Prevention and combat against sexual harassment at the workplace; order and procedures for handling sexual harassment at the workplace;
Employees’ violations of labor discipline, forms of dealing with violations of labor discipline;
Material responsibility;
Persons competent to handle violations of labor discipline

Before issuing the internal working regulations or amending and supplementing the internal working regulations, an employer shall consult the representative organization of the grassroots-level employees in the case there is a representative organization of the grassroots-level employees
The internal working regulations must be notified to employees and their key contents must be displayed at necessary places in the workplace
The Government shall detail this Article
Article 119. Registration of internal working regulations
An employer employing 10 or more employees shall register its internal working regulations with a labor agency under the provincial People's Committee where the employer registers its business
Within 10 days from the date of issuance of the internal working regulations, an employer shall submit a dossier for registration of the internal working regulations

Within 07 working days from the date of receipt of a dossier for registration of the internal working regulations, if the internal working regulations have contents contrary to law, the labor agency under the provincial People's Committee shall notify and instruct the employer to amend, supplement and re-register

In case an employer has branches, units, production and business establishments located in different areas, he/she shall send the registered internal working regulations to the labor agency under the provincial People's Committee where the branches, units and production and business establishments are located

Based on specific conditions, the labor agency under the provincial-level People's Committee may authorize the labor agency of the district-level People's Committee to register internal working regulations under this Article
Article 120. Dossier for registration of internal working regulations
An application for registration of the internal working regulations;
The internal working regulations;
Minutes of comments of the representative organization of the grassroots-level employees in the case there is a representative organization of the grassroots-level employees;
Documents of the employer related to labor discipline and material responsibilities (if any)
Article 121. Validity of internal working regulations
Article 122. Principles, order and procedures for handling violations of labor discipline
The handling of a violation of labor discipline is provided as follows
The employer must prove the employee's fault;
The representative organization of the grassroots-level employees where the employee being disciplined is a member must participate in the handling;

The employee must be present and may defend himself/herself or ask a lawyer or a representative organization of employees to defend him/her; if the employee is under 15 years old, his/her at-law representative must participate in the handling;
The handling of the violation of labor discipline must be recorded in the minutes
It shall be prohibited to impose more than one form of discipline for a single violation of labor discipline
In case an employee simultaneously commits more than one violation of labor discipline, it shall be only allowed to apply the highest form of discipline corresponding to the most serious violation
Labor discipline may not be imposed for violations committed by an employee who is currently
Taking sickness or convalescence leave or a leave with the employer’s consent;
Kept in custody or temporary detention;
Waiting for results of verification and conclusion of a competent agency for acts of violation specified in Clauses 1 and 2, Article 125 of this Code;
A pregnant female employee; an employee taking maternity leave or rearing a child under 12 months of age

Labor discipline shall not be imposed on an employee who violates the internal working regulations while suffering a mental disorder or another disease which deprives him/her of the capacity to perceive or control his/her acts
The Government shall specify the order and procedures for handling of violations of labor discipline
Article 123. Statute of limitations for handling violations of labor discipline

The statute of limitations for handling a violation of labor discipline is 6 months from the date the violation is committed. The statute of limitations for handling a violation of labor discipline directly related to finance and assets or disclosure of technological or business secrets is 12 months

Upon expiry of the period specified in Clause 4, Article 122 of this Code, if the statute of limitations for handling violations of labor discipline has expired or still remained valid but less than 60 days, it may be extended to handle violations of labor discipline but for no more than 60 days from the expiry date mentioned above
The employer shall issue a decision on handle violations of labor discipline within the time limits specified in Clauses 1 and 2 of this Article
Article 124. Forms of handling of violations of labor discipline
Reprimand
Prolongation of the wage rise period for no more than 06 months
Demotion
Dismissal
Article 125. Application of dismissal as a form of discipline
An employee commits an act of theft, embezzlement, gambling, intentional infliction of injury, use of drugs inside the workplace;

An employee commits an act of disclosing technological or business secrets or causing serious damage or threatening to cause serious damage to the assets or interests of the employer; sexual harassment at the workplace as stipulated in the internal working regulations;

An employee who has been subject to the disciplinary measure of prolonging the wage rise period or dismissing commits recidivism when the disciplinary record has not yet been written off. Recidivism means that an employee re-commits the same violation for which he/she has been disciplined while his/her disciplinary record has not yet been written off as prescribed in Article 126 of this Code;
An employee has been absent from work without permission for a total of 05 working days within 30 days or 20 days within 365 days without plausible reasons
Article 126. Writing off of disciplinary records, reduction of the duration of labor discipline

After 03 months from the date of being reprimanded or after 06 months from the date of being disciplined by prolonging the wage rise period or after 03 years from the date of being disciplined for dismissal, if an employee does not commit recidivism, his/her disciplinary record be automatically written off

An employee who is subject to the disciplinary measure of prolonging the wage rise period and has served half of the duration of the discipline may be considered by the employer for a reduction of such duration if showing progress
Article 127. Prohibited acts when handling violations of labor discipline
Infringing upon the employees' health, honor, life, prestige and dignity
Applying a fine or wage reduction instead of a disciplinary measure
Disciplining an employee who has committed a violation which is not defined in the internal working regulations or not agreed upon in signed the labor contract or not prescribed in the labor code
Article 128. Work suspension

An employer may suspend an employee from working if the employer considers that the case of violation is complex and any continued performance of the work by the employee can cause difficulties to verification work. Work suspension may only be applied after having consulting the representative organization of the grassroots-level employees where the employee under consideration for suspension is a member

The period of work suspension must not exceed 15 days, or 90 days in special cases. During the period of work suspension, the employee shall be entitled to 50 per cent of the wage he/she receives prior to the suspension
In case the employee is disciplined, he/she is not required to reimburse the wage advanced to him/her
In case the employee is not disciplined, the employer shall pay the full wage for the period of work suspension
Section 2
MATERIAL RESPONSIBILITIES
Article 129. Compensation for damage
An employee who causes damage to tools and equipment or the assets of the employer shall pay compensation in accordance with law or the employer’s internal working regulations

An employee who loses tools, equipment or assets of the employer or other assets assigned to him/her by the employer, or uses supplies in excess of the permitted norms shall compensate the whole or a part of the damage at the market price; in case a contract of responsibility has been signed, the amount of compensation must comply with such contract; in case the damage is caused by a natural disaster, fire, enemy sabotage, epidemic, calamity or another objective event which is unforeseeable and irremediable and every necessary measure has been taken to full ability, no compensation is required
Article 130. Handling of damage compensation
Consideration and decision on the levels of compensation must be based on the fault, the actual level of damage, the actual family conditions, personal records and property of the employee concerned
The Government shall specify the order, procedures and statute of limitations for handling of damage compensation
Article 131. Complaints about labor discipline and material responsibilities
Chapter IX
OCCUPATIONAL SAFETY AND HYGIENE
Article 132. Compliance with the law on occupational safety and hygiene
Article 133. Occupational safety and hygiene program
The Government decides the national Program on occupational safety and sanitation

Provincial-level People’s Committees shall submit local occupational safety and hygiene programs to the same-level People Councils for decision, and include them in their socio-economic development plans
Article 134. Assurance of occupational safety and hygiene at workplace
An employer shall assume responsibility for fully implementing measures to ensure occupational safety and hygiene at the workplace

An employee shall assume responsibility for observing the regulations, internal rules, procedures and requirements on occupational safety and hygiene; complying with law and mastering the knowledge and skills of measures to ensure occupational safety and hygiene at the workplace
Chapter X
SEPARATE PROVISIONS FOR FEMALE EMPLOYEES AND ENSURING GENDER EQUALITY
Article 135. State policies
Ensuring the female and male employees’ rights to employment equality, taking measures to ensure gender equality, preventing and combating against sexual harassment at the workplace
Encouraging employers to create conditions for female and male employees to have regular employment, extensively implementing systems of flexible working hours, part-time work or home-based work

Taking measures to create employment opportunities, improve working conditions, raise vocational qualifications and healthcare, and increase material and spiritual welfare for female employees in order to assist them in effectively bringing into play their vocational capacity and harmoniously combining their working lives with family lives
Formulating policies on tax reductions for employers using many female employees in accordance with tax laws

The State shall develop plans and measures to organize crèches and kindergartens in areas with large numbers of employees. Developing various forms of training which are favorable for female employees to acquire standby vocational skills suitable to their physical and physiological characteristics and their motherhood function
The Government shall detail this Article
Article 136. Responsibilities of employers
Ensuring gender equality and implementing measures to promote gender equality in recruitment, employment, training, working time, rest time, wages and other policies
Consulting female employees or their representatives when taking decisions on issues related to the rights and interests of women
Ensuring sufficient bathrooms and appropriate toilets in the workplace
Assisting and supporting in building crèches and kindergartens, or covering part of childcare expenses at crèches and kindergartens incurred by female employees
Article 137. Protection of maternity for female employees
An employer may not mobilize employees to work at night, work overtime or go on a long working trip in the following cases
The employee is in her seventh month of pregnancy, or in her sixth month of pregnancy in case of working in a mountainous, remote, distant, border or island area;
The employee is nursing a child under 12 months of age

In case a female employee is engaged in heavy, hazardous, dangerous or extremely heavy, hazardous, dangerous work or work adversely affecting the reproductive and child-rearing function during her pregnancy and notifies the employer, she shall be entitled to be transferred to a lighter and safer work or have her daily working time reduced by 01 hour without any reductions in wages, rights and interests until the end of nursing a child under 12 months of age

An employer may neither dismiss a female employee nor unilaterally terminate the labor contract with a female employee for the reason of her marriage, pregnancy, maternity leave, or that she is nursing a child under 12 months of age, except the case in which the employer is an individual who dies, or is declared by a court to have lost his/her civil act capacity, or to be missing or dead, or the employer is not an individual terminating operation or is notified by a business registration agency of the provincial People's Committee that there is no legal representative, authorized person to exercise the rights and obligations of the legal representative

A female employee in her menstruation period shall be entitled to a 30-minute break in every working day; a female employee nursing a child under 12 months of age shall be entitled to a 60-minute break in every working day with full wage as stated in the labor contract
Article 138. Right of pregnant employees to unilaterally terminate or postpone labor contracts

In case a pregnant employee has a certificate of a competent health treatment and examination establishment which states that continued work will adversely affect her pregnancy, she may unilaterally terminate the labor contract or temporarily postpone the performance of the labor contract

In case of temporarily postponing the performance of the labor contract, the period of postponement shall be agreed upon by the employee with the employer but must be at least equal to the time designated by the competent health examination and treatment establishment. In case there is no designation of the competent health examination and treatment establishment regarding the time of temporary leave, the two parties shall agree on the time of temporarily postponing the performance of the labor contract
Article 139. Maternity leave
A female employee is entitled to 06 months of prenatal and postnatal leave; prenatal leave must not exceed 02 months
During the maternity leave, a female employee shall be entitled to maternity policies provided by the law on social insurance
After the maternity leave period stipulated in Clause 1 of this Article, if a female employee wishes, she may take additional leave without pay after agreed upon with the employer

Before the expiration of her maternity leave stipulated in Clause 1 of this Article, a female employee may return to work after having taken at leas04 months of maternity leave but she must give advance notice to the employer and agreed by her employer. She also must have a certificate from a competent health treatment and examination establishment that early resumption of work will not adversely affect her health. In this case, the female employee continues to receive the maternity allowance as provided by the law on social insurance, in addition to the wage paid by the employer for her working days

For a male employee when his wife gives birth, an employee who adopts children less than 06 months of age, a female employee who is a surrogate mother and an employee who is a mother requesting surrogacy shall be entitled to take the maternity leave as provided by the law on social insurance
Article 140. Employment guarantee for employees after maternity leave
Article 141. Allowances for leave for caring a sick child, for pregnancy checks-up and for applying contraceptive measures
Article 142. Occupations and work adversely affecting child bearing and nursing functions
The Minister of Labor, War Invalids and Social Affairs shall promulgate a list of occupations and work that are harmful to child bearing and nursing functions

The employer must provide sufficient information on the work’s dangerous nature, risks and requirements for the employees to choose and must ensure the occupational safety and hygiene conditions for the employees in accordance with regulations when employing them for the work on the list specified in Clause 1 of this Article
Chapter XI
PRIVACY PROVISIONS FOR LABOR
MINORS AND SOME OTHER EMPLOYEES
Section 1
MINOR EMPLOYEES
Article 143. Minor employees
A minor employee is an employee under 18 years of age
Persons aged between full 15 and under 18 may not work or work at workplaces prescribed in Article 147 of this Code
Persons aged between full 13 and under 15 may only perform light jobs according to the list promulgated by the Minister of Labor, War Invalids and Social Affairs
Persons aged under 13 may only perform the jobs specified in Clause 3, Article 145 of this Code
Article 144. Principles of employment of minor employees
A minor employee may only perform jobs suitable to his/her health to ensure physical, mental and personality development
An employer, when employing minor employees, shall assume the responsibility to take care of employees in terms of labor, health, and study in the labor process

When employing minor employees, an employer must have the consent of their parents or guardians; make a separate monitoring book, record full name, date of birth, current job, results of periodical health checks, and shall present it at the request of a competent state agency
An employer must create opportunities for minor employees to learn cultural, vocational education, train, foster and improve occupational skills qualifications
Article 145. Use of employees aged under 15 years
When employing persons under 15 years of age to work, an employer must comply with the following provisions
To sign a labor contract in writing with a person under 15 years of age and his/her legal representative;
To arrange working hours without affecting the learning time of persons under 15 years of age;

To have a health certificate issued by a competent health facility certifying the health of persons under 15 years of age suitable to their jobs and to organize periodical health checks at least once every 06 months;
To ensure working conditions, occupational safety, and sanitation suitable for ages
An employer shall only recruit and employ persons aged between full 13 and under 15 to perform light jobs as prescribed in Clause 3, Article 143 of this Code

Recruitment and employment of persons aged under 13 years is prohibited, except for art, physical training and sports jobs without prejudice to physical, mental and human development and must have the consent of a labor agency of the provincial-level People's Committee
The Minister of Labor, War Invalids and Social Affairs shall detail this Article
Article 146. Working time of minors
The working time of persons under 15 years must not exceed 04 hours in 01 day and 20 hours in 01 weeks; and the employer may not employ these minors to work overtime or at night

The working time of a person aged from full 15 to less than 18 must not exceed 08 hours in a day and 40 hours in a week. Persons aged between full 15 and under 18 may work overtime and work at night in a number of occupations and jobs on the list promulgated by the Minister of Labor, War Invalids and Social Affairs
Article 147. Prohibited jobs and workplaces for employees aged between full 15 and under 18 years
Employment of persons aged between full 15 and under 18 is prohibited in the following jobs
Carrying and lifting heavy objects which are beyond a minor’s physical strength;
Producing and trading in alcohol, wine, beer, cigarettes, substances affecting the spirit or other addictive substances;
Producing, using or transporting chemicals, gases, explosives;
Maintenance of equipment and machinery;
Demolition of construction works;
Scuba diving, fishing, and offshore fishing;
Other jobs that are harmful the physical, mental and personality development of minors
Employment of persons aged full 15 to under 18 years is prohibited in the following workplaces
Underwater, underground, in caves and in tunnels;
Construction site;
Animal slaughter facilities;
Casinos, bars, dance halls, karaoke parlors, hotels, hostels, saunas, massage parlors; lottery business points, electronic game services;
Other workplaces which are harmful to the physical, mental and personality development of minor employees
The Minister of Labor, War Invalids and Social Affairs shall specify the lists at Point h, Clause 1 and Point dd, Clause 2 of this Article
Section 2
ELDERLY EMPLOYEES
Article 148. Elderly employees
An elderly employee is a person who continues to work after the age prescribed in Clause 2, Article 169 of this Code
Elderly employees shall be entitled to agree with employers on reducing daily working hours or applying part-time working regimes
The State encourages the employment of elderly employees to work in conformity with their health to ensure labor rights and efficient use of human resources
Article 149. Employment of elderly employees
When employing an elderly employee, the two parties may agree to enter into several definite-term labor contracts

When the elderly employee who is enjoying the pension prescribed in the Law on Social Insurance works under a new labor contract, in addition to the benefits he/she is entitled to under the retirement regime, he/she is entitled to the salaries and other benefits in accordance with the law and labor contracts

It is prohibited to employ elderly employees to perform heavy, hazardous, dangerous or extremely heavy, hazardous, dangerous jobs, which adversely affect the health of elderly employees, except for the cases that ensure safe working conditions
Employers shall be responsible for taking care of the health of elderly employees at the workplace
Section 3
VIETNAMESE EMPLOYEES WORKING ABROAD, EMPLOYEES OF FOREIGN ORGANIZATIONS AND INDIVIDUALS IN VIETNAM, FOREIGN EMPLOYEES WORKING IN VIETNAM
Article 150. Vietnamese employees working abroad, employees of foreign organizations and individuals in Vietnam
The State encourages enterprises, agencies, organizations, and individuals to seek and expand the labor market in order to send Vietnamese employees to work abroad

Vietnamese citizens working for foreign organizations in Vietnam, in industrial parks, economic zones, export processing zones, hi-tech parks or working for individuals who are foreign citizens in Vietnam shall abide by Vietnamese laws and are protected by law
The Government shall detail the recruitment and management of Vietnamese employees working for foreign organizations and individuals in Vietnam
Article 151. Conditions for foreign citizens to work in Vietnam
A foreign citizen working in Vietnam is foreign nationals and must meet the following conditions
Being 18 years of age or older and having full civil act capacity;
Having professional qualifications, techniques, work skills, and work experience; have good health as prescribed by the Minister of Health;
Not being a person who is serving a penalty or has not had his/her criminal record remitted or is being examined for penal liability in accordance with foreign law or Vietnamese law;
Having a work permit granted by a competent Vietnamese state agency, except for the case specified in Article 154 of this Code

The term of a labor contract for foreign citizens working in Vietnam must not exceed the term of the work permit. When employing foreign citizens working in Vietnam, the two parties may agree to enter into several definite-term labor contracts
Foreign citizens working in Vietnam must abide by the Vietnamese labor law and are protected by Vietnamese law, unless otherwise provided by treaties to which Vietnam is a contracting party
Article 152. Conditions for recruiting and employing foreign employees to work in Vietnam

Enterprises, agencies, organizations, individuals, and contractors may only recruit foreign citizens in such positions as manager, managing director, expert and technical employee which Vietnamese employees are still unable to fill to meet production and business requirements

Enterprises, agencies, organizations, and individuals shall, before recruiting foreign citizens to work in the territory of Vietnam, explain their labor demands and obtain written approval of the competent state agencies

Contractors shall, before recruiting and employing foreign citizens to work in the territory of Vietnam, declare in detail the job positions, professional and technical qualifications, working experience and working time that need to use foreign employees to execute the bidding package and obtain the written approval of the competent state agency
Article 153. Responsibilities of employers and foreign employees
Foreign employees must present work permits at the request of competent state agencies
Foreign employees working in Vietnam without a work permit shall be forced to leave Vietnam or be deported in accordance with the law on entry, exit, transit, and residence of foreigners in Vietnam
Employers who employ foreign employees to work for themselves without work permits shall be handled according to the provisions of law
Article 154. Foreign employees working in Vietnam are not eligible for work permits
Being the owner or capital contributing member of a limited liability company with the value of capital contribution under the Government's regulations
Being the Chairman of the Board of Directors or a member of the Board of Directors of a joint-stock company with the value of capital contribution as prescribed by the Government
Being the head of a representative office or project or responsible primarily for the operation of international organizations and foreign non-governmental organizations in Vietnam
Entering Vietnam with a term of less than 03 months to conduct service offerings

Entering Vietnam for less than 03 months to deal with incidents, complicated technical and technological situations that affect or threaten to affect production and business activities of Vietnamese experts and foreign experts currently in Vietnam cannot handle it
Being a foreign lawyer who has been granted a law practice license in Vietnam in accordance with the Law on Lawyers
The cases in accordance with the provisions of international treaties to which the Socialist Republic of Vietnam is a member
Foreigners marrying Vietnamese and living in the Vietnamese territory
Other cases as prescribed by the Government
Article 155. Validity duration of work permits
Article 156. Cases of termination of validity of work permits
The work permit expires
The labor contract terminates
The content of the labor contract is not consistent with the content of the granted work permit
Working not in accordance with the contents of the issued work permit
The contracts in the domains that are the basis for generating work permits which are expired or terminated
There is a written notice of the foreign party quitting the appointment of a foreign employee to work in Vietnam
Enterprises, organizations, partners of the Vietnamese side or foreign organizations in Vietnam employing foreign employees to terminate their operations
The work permit is revoked
Article 157. Issuance, re-issuance, extension, and revocation of work permits, certifications not subject to work permits
Section 4
DISABLED EMPLOYEES
Article 158. State policies for disabled employees
Article 159. Employment of disabled persons
An employer shall ensure working conditions, working tools, occupational safety and hygiene, and organize periodical health checks suitable for disabled employees
An employer shall consult disabled employees before deciding on matters involving their rights and interests
Article 160. Prohibited acts in employment of disabled persons

Employing an employee with mild disability who has lost 51% or more of his/her working ability, an employee with severe disability or extremely severe disability to work overtime or at night, except for cases when obtaining the disabled employee’s consents

Employing a disabled employee to perform a heavy, hazardous and dangerous job on the list promulgated by the Minister of Labor, War Invalids and Social Affairs without the consent of the disabled person after the employer has provided all the information about the job
Section 5
DOMESTIC EMPLOYEES
Article 161. Domestic employees
Domestic employee is a person who regularly does housework for one or more families
The Government shall prescribe regulations on domestic employees
Article 162. Labor contracts for domestic employees
An employer shall engage in a written labor contract with a domestic employee
The duration of a labor contract for a domestic employee may be negotiated by both parties. Either party may unilaterally terminate the labor contract with an advance notice of 15 days
Both sides shall clearly specify the form of wage payment and the terms of payment, daily working hours and accommodation in the labor contract
Article 163. Obligations of an employer employing domestic employee(s)
To fully implement the agreements in the labor contract
To pay to the domestic employee an amount of his/her social insurance and health insurance as provided by law to enable the employee to self-manage his/her insurance
To respect the honor and dignity of the domestic employee
To provide a clean and hygienic accommodation for the domestic employee if so agreed
To create opportunities for the domestic employee to receive education and vocational training
To pay travel expenses for the domestic employee to return home at the end of his/her service, except the case in which the domestic employee terminates the labor contract ahead of time
Article 164. Obligations of a domestic employee
To fully implement the agreements in the labor contract
To pay compensation as agreed upon or provided by law in case of damaging or losing any property of the employer
To timely notify the employer of any possibilities and risks of accident, safety, health, life and property of the employer’s family and his/her own
To denounce to competent agencies if the employer commits acts of mistreating, sexually harassing or forcing labor or any other illegal acts
Article 165. Prohibited acts of employers
Mistreating, sexually harassing, forcing labor and using violence against the domestic employee
Assigning work to the domestic employees not in accordance with the labor contract
Keeping personal documents of the domestic employee
SECTION 6
OTHER TYPES OF EMPLOYEES
Article 166. Persons working in the fields of art, physical training, sports, maritime and aviation
Article 167. Employees performing home-based work
CHAPTER XII
SOCIAL INSURANCE, HEALTH INSURANCE AND UNEMPLOYEMENT INSURANCE
Article 168. Participation in social insurance, health insurance and unemployment insurance

Employers and employees shall participate in compulsory social insurance, health insurance and unemployment insurance and are entitled to the benefits in accordance with the social insurance, health insurance and unemployment insurance laws
When an employee is absent from work and is covered by social insurance, the employer is not required to pay a wage to the employee, unless otherwise agreed by both parties

For an employee who is not covered by compulsory social insurance, health insurance and unemployment insurance, the employer shall concurrently pay to the employee a wage and an amount which is equivalent to the level of contribution to compulsory social insurance, compulsory health insurance and unemployment insurance in accordance with the social insurance, health insurance and unemployment insurance laws
Article 169. Age of retirement
An employee, who meets the conditions on the period of payment of social insurance as prescribed by the law on social insurance, is entitled to a pension when reaching the age of retirement

The age of retirement for employees in normal working conditions shall be amended in accordance with the roadmap until male employees reach full 62 years old in 2028 and female employees reach full 60 years old in 2035

An employee whose working capacity has been declined; who performs a specially heavy, hazardous or dangerous job or a heavy, hazardous or dangerous job; who works in a region facing exceptionally difficult socio-economic conditions shall be entitled to retire at a younger age, but shall not be more than 05 years earlier than the age defined in Clause 2 of this Article at the time of retirement, unless otherwise prescribed by the law

An employee who has high professional and technical qualifications and other special cases may retire at an older age, but shall not be more than 05 years higher than the age specified in Clause 2 of this Article at the time of retirement, unless otherwise prescribed by the law
The Government shall detail the regulations of this Article
CHAPTER XIII
WORKERS’ REPRESENTATIVE ORGANIZATIONS
AT GRASSROOT LEVEL
Article 170. The right to establish, join and operate workers’ representative organizations at grassroot level
Employees shall have the right to establish, join and operate trade unions in accordance with the Law on Trade Union
Employees of enterprises have the right to establish, join and operate the organization of employees at the enterprise as defined in Article 172, Article 173 and Article 174 of this Code

Workers’ representative organizations as prescribed in Clause 1 and Clause 2 of this Article shall have equal rights and obligations in representing and protecting lawful rights and legitimate interests of employees in industrial relations
Article 171. Grassroot-level trade unions under the system of Vietnam trade unions
Grassroots-level trade unions under the system of Vietnam trade unions shall be established in agencies, organizations, units and enterprises
The establishment, dissolution, organization and operation of grassroots-level trade unions shall be conducted in accordance with the Law on Trade Unions
Article 172. The establishment and participation of workers’ representative organization at an enterprise
A workers’ representative organization at an enterprise shall be established and operated after a competent state agency grants it the registration

The registration of the workers’ representative organization at an enterprise shall be revoked if the organization violates principles and purposes of the organization as prescribed at Point b, Clause 1, Article 174 of this Code or if the workers’ representative organization at the enterprise cease to exist in cases of division, separation, consolidation, merging, or dissolution or the enterprise undergoes dissolution or bankruptcy
In case that the workers’ representative organization at the enterprise join the Vietnam Trade union, the organization shall conform to regulations of the Law on Trade Unions

The Government shall prescribe the dossier; competence and procedure for registration, procedure for granting registration, or revoking registration; shall perform state management on the finance and assets of workers’ representative organizations at enterprises; and shall prescribe the unification, mergence, separation, segregation and dissolution of such organizations
Article 173. Board of leaders, and members of workers’ representative organization at an enterprise

At the time of registration, the workers’ representative organization at an enterprise shall gain the minimum threshold of membership working at the enterprise as prescribed by the Government’s regulations

The board of leaders shall be elected by members of the workers’ representative organization at the enterprise. Members of the elected board of the workers’ representative organizations at the enterprise shall be Vietnamese employees who are working at the enterprise, are not in the period of penal liability examination or executing the punishment, and are not in the period when their recorded unspent offences have not been released due to committing any crimes against national security; crimes against freedom of human beings, crimes of infringement upon citizens’ democratic freedom; crimes against ownership rights in accordance with regulations prescribed in the Penal Code
Article 174. Constitution of the workers’ representative organization at an enterprise
Constitution of the workers’ representative organization at an enterprise shall include the following main contents
Name and address of the organization; symbol (if any)

Mandate, purposes and scope of organization shall be to protect lawful rights and legitimate interests of members of the organization in industrial relations at the enterprise; to resolve issues, together with employers, related to rights, obligations and interests of employees and employers; to establish a progressive, harmonious and stable industrial relations;
Requirements and procedures to join and withdraw from the workers’ representative organization at an enterprise
Organizational structure, working tenure and representatives of organization;
Procedures for the adoption of decisions of the organization;
Membership fees, source of property and finance, and its usage and management of the organization
Complaints and internal resolutions for complaints;
The Government shall detail regulations of this Article
Article 175. Prohibited acts of employers related to the establishment, participation and operation of workers’ representative organizations at grassroot level

Acts of discrimination against employees and members of workers’ representative organizations for the reason of establishment, joining and operation of workers’ representative organizations, including
Requesting employees to join or not to join or to leave the workers’ representative organization as a requirement for their recruitment, engagement or extension of labor contracts;
Dismissing, disciplining, unilaterally terminating employment contracts, or rejecting to extend labor contracts or transferring employees to perform other jobs;
Discriminating over wages, working hours and other rights and obligations in the extent of industrial relations;
Creating obstacles and difficulties in works in order to obstruct the operation of workers’ representative organizations at grassroot level

Acts of interference and manipulation in the process of establishment, election, development of work plan and implementation of activities of workers’ representative organizations, including using financial support or using economic measures to undermine or weaken the functioning and performance of workers’ representative organizations at grassroot level or to discriminate in favor of or against workers’ representative organizations at grassroot level
Article 176. Rights of members of the Board of leaders of workers’ representative organizations at grassroot level
Members of the Board of leaders of workers’ representative organizations at grassroot level are entitled to the following rights

To meet employees at workplace when they perform tasks of workers’ representative organizations. It must be ensured that the performing such tasks shall not have any effect on the normal operation of employers;
To meet employers to perform tasks representing workers’ representative organizations at grassroot level;
To allocate their working time, as prescribed in Clause 2 and Clause 3 of this Article, to perform tasks of workers’ representative organizations while remaining to be paid by the employers;
To be provided with guarantees in industrial relations and in the implementation of their representative functions in accordance with the law

The Government shall prescribe the minimum time that an employer must share allocate all members of the Board of leaders of the workers’ representative organization at grass-root level to perform tasks of the organization on the basis of the number of members of this organization

The workers’ representative organization at grassroot level and the employer shall negotiate about the additional time compared to the minimum time specified in Clause 2 of this Article and the way to use the working time for members of the Board of leaders of the workers’ representative organization at grassroot level in line with their actual conditions
Article 177. Obligations of employers towards workers’ representative organizations at grassroot level

To create no obstructions and difficulties when employees conduct lawful activities to establish, join a workers’ representative organization and participate in the operation of this workers’ representative organization at grassroot level
To recognize and respect rights of legally established workers’ representative organizations

To reach written agreements with the Board of leaders of workers’ representative organizations in case where the employers unilaterally terminate employment contracts or transfer employees to perform other jobs or apply disciplinary measure of dismissal to employees who are elected members of the Board of leaders of workers’ representative organizations. If failing to reach such agreement, the two parties shall report to competent agencies on labor issues under provincial People’s Committee. After 30 days from the date of reporting to competent agencies on labor issues under provincial People’s Committee, employers shall be eligible for making decisions. If disagreeing with the decision of the employers, employees and the Board of leaders of workers’ representative organizations have the right to request labor dispute settlement in line with the procedure and order prescribed by the law

To extend the labor contracts until the end of their working tenure for employees whose labor contracts expire while they are in the incumbent Board of leaders of a workers’ representative organization
To perform other obligations in accordance with the law
Article 178. Rights and obligations of workers’ representative organizations at grassroot level in industrial relations
To conduct collective bargaining with employers in accordance with regulations of this Code;
To participate in dialogues at workplace in accordance with regulations of this Code;

To consult over the formation and supervision of the implementation of wage scales, wage tables, determination of labor norms, wage payment regulations, bonus regulations, internal working regulations and other relevant issues related to the rights and obligations of employees who are members of the organizations
To represent employees in labor disputes and in complaint resolution upon authorization of employees;
To organize and lead strikes under regulations of this Code;

To receive technical support of legally-operated agencies and organizations in Viet Nam for the comprehension of the Labor law, of formalities and procedures of the establishment of workers’ representative organizations and of performance of their representative activities in industrial relations after being granted registration
To be provided by employers with a workspace, information, and to be given guarantees for necessary conditions for the operation of workers’ representative organizations
To be entitled to other rights and obligations in line with the law
CHAPTER XIV
SETTLEMENT OF LABOR DISPUTES
Section 1
GENERAL PROVISIONS ON THE SETTLEMENT
OF LABOR DISPUTES
Article 179. Labor disputes

Labor dispute is a dispute on rights, obligations and interests that arise among the parties in the process of establishing, implementing or terminating labor relations; or a dispute among worker’s representative organizations; or a dispute arising from relations that are directly related to industrial relations. Labor disputes shall include the following categories

Individual labor disputes between an employer and an employee; between an employee and an enterprise or agency that sends the employee to work overseas on work contract; between a dispatched employee and a hiring party;
Right-based and interest-based collective labor disputes between one or several workers’ representative organizations and an employer or one or more employers’ organization(s);

A right-based collective labor dispute is a dispute between one or several workers’ representative organization(s) and an employer or one or more employers’ organization(s) that arises in the following cases
Difference in the interpretation and the implementation of terms in collective bargaining agreements, internal working regulations, and other regulations and other lawful agreements;
Difference in the interpretation and the implementation of the labor law;

When an employer engages in an act of discrimination against employees, rank-and-file members and members of the Board of leaders of workers’ representative organizations for the reason of establishing and joining workers’ representative organizations and participating in workers’ representative organizations activities; or when an employer engages in an act of intervention or manipulation against workers’ representative organizations; or in an act of violation of the obligation to negotiate in good faith
Right-based collective labor disputes shall include
Labor disputes that arise during the process of collective bargaining;
When one party refuses to negotiate or does not conduct negotiations within the time limit as prescribed by the law
Article 180. Principles of settlement of labor disputes
To respect the self-determination right through negotiation of the parties throughout the labor dispute settlement process

To attach great importance to the settlement of labor disputes through mediation and arbitration on the basis of respect for the rights and interests of both disputing parties, of respect for the common interest of the society and the compliance with the law;
To guarantee publicity, transparency, objectiveness, timeliness, quickness and lawfulness
To ensure the participation of representative sof each party in the labor dispute settlement process

The settlement of a labor dispute shall be conducted by a competent agency, organization or person upon request from the disputing parties or upon request from competent agencies, organizations and individuals and agreed by the disputing parties
Article 181. Responsibilities of agencies and organizations in the settlement of labor disputes

The state management agency of labor shall coordinate with the workers’ representative organization and the employers’ representative organization in providing guidance and assistance to the disputing parties during the labor dispute settlement
The Ministry of Labor, War Invalids and Social Affairs shall organize training to raise professional capacity for labor conciliators and arbitrators in settling labor disputes

Upon request for labor dispute settlement, competent agencies on labor under People’s Committee shall be the focal point to receive the request for labor disputes settlement, shall take the responsibility for classifying, providing guidance and support to the disputing parties in the labor dispute settlement
Article 182. Rights and obligations of the two disputing parties in labor dispute settlement
During the labor dispute settlement, the two parties have the following rights
To participate directly or through a representative in the settlement process;
To withdraw or change the content of their written request;
To request change of the person in charge of settling the labor dispute if they have grounds to believe that such person may not be impartial or objective
During the labor dispute settlement, the two disputing parties shall have the following obligations
To promptly and fully provide all documents and evidence to prove their request;
To abide by the reached agreement, the judgment of the Board of Labor Conciliators or the ruling of People’s Court which has taken legal effect
Article 183. Powers of competent agencies, organizations and individuals in the settlement of labor disputes
Article 184. Labor conciliators

Labor conciliators are appointed by the Chairperson of a provincial People’s Committee to conciliate labor disputes, and disputes over vocational training contracts; and to support the development of industrial relations

The Government shall prescribe the criteria, procedures and formalities for the appointment of conciliators; working conditions and management of labor conciliators; and competence, procedures and formalities for sending labor conciliators
Article 185. Labor Arbitration Council

The chairperson of a provincial-level People’s Committee shall decide to establish the Labor Arbitration Council and to appoint its Chairperson, a secretary and labor arbitrators of the Labor Arbitration Council. The working term of the Labor Arbitration Council shall be 5 years

The number of arbitrators of the Labor Arbitration Council shall be decided by the Chairperson of the provincial People’s Committee, consisting of at least 15 members, including equal proportions nominated by each party, specifically

At least 05 members nominated by the competent agency on labor under the provincial People’s Committee, of which the Chairperson of the Council is the representative leader from this agency and the Council secretary is an official of this agency
At least 05 members nominated by the provincial federation of labor;
At least 05 members nominated by employers’ representative organizations in the province
Criteria and working regime of labor arbitrators shall be prescribed as follows
Labor arbitrators must have knowledge of laws, experiences in industrial relations, and must be creditable and impartial;

When nominating labor arbitrators under regulations in Clause 2 of this Article, the competent agency on labor under the provincial People’s Committee, the provincial federation of labor, and employers’ representative organizations may nominate their officials and other people meeting the criteria of labor arbitrators under legal regulations;
The Secretary of the Labor Arbitration Council shall work full-time at the Labor Arbitration Council. Labor arbitrators may work on full-time or part-time basis

Upon a request to settle labor disputes under regulations in Article 189, Article 193 and Article 197 of this Code, the Labor Arbitration Council shall establish an Arbitration Panel to settle labor disputes as follows
Representative of each disputing party shall select one arbitrator in the list of labor arbitrators
Labor arbitrators selected by disputing parties as prescribed at Point a of this Clause shall nominate 01 other labor arbitrator to be the Head of the Arbitration Panel;
In case all disputing parties select the same arbitrator to settle labor disputes, the Arbitration Panel shall include only 01 arbitrator;
The Arbitration Panel shall operate on the principle of collectivism and the rule of majority, except for cases specified at Point c, Clause 4 of this Article;

The Government shall prescribe in details for the criteria, procedures, and formalities for the appointment and dismissal of arbitrators, working conditions for labor arbitrators and the Labor Arbitration Council; the establishment and operation of the Labor Arbitration Council; and the organization and operation of the Arbitration Panel as defined at this Article
Article 186. Prohibition of unilateral acts pending settlement of labor disputes
SECTION 2
COMPETENCE AND PROCEDURES FOR THE SETTLEMENT OF INDIVIDUAL LABOR DISPUTES
Article 187. Competence for the settlement of individual labor disputes
The Labor conciliator;
The Labor Arbitration Council;
The People’s Court
Article 188. Procedures for the settlement of individual labor disputes by labor conciliators

Individual labor disputes must go through the conciliation conducted by labor conciliators before going to the Labour Arbitration Council or the People’s court for settlement, except the following labor disputes
Disputes over disciplinary measures of dismissal or unilateral termination of labor contracts;
Disputes over compensation for damage and allowance upon termination of labor contracts;
Disputes between a domestic employee and his/her employer;

Disputes over social insurance in accordance with the law on social insurance, disputes over health insurance in accordance with the law on health insurance, disputes over unemployment insurance in accordance with the law on employment, disputes over insurance against work accident or occupational disease in accordance with the law on occupational safety and hygiene;
Disputes between dispatched employees and their employers;

Within 05 working days from the date of receiving a conciliation request from disputing parties or from competent agencies as defined in Clause 3, Article 181 of this Code, the labor conciliator shall complete the conciliation
Both disputing parties must be present at the conciliation meeting. The disputing parties may authorize their representatives to attend the conciliation meeting
The labor conciliator shall instruct and support the disputing parties to negotiate and settle disputes
Copies of the record of successful or unsuccessful conciliation must be sent to all disputing parties within 01 working day from the date the record is made

In case either party does not implement the agreement written in the record of successful conciliation, the other disputing party has the right to request settlement by the Labor Arbitration Council or a court

In case where conciliation is not required as specified at Clause 1 of this Article or where the labor conciliator fails to resolve the disputes within the time limits as prescribed in Clause 2 of this Article or in case of unsuccessful conciliation as specified in Clause 4 of this Article, the disputing parties shall have the right to choose one of the following methods to settle labor disputes
To request the Arbitration Council for settlement as prescribed in Article 189 of this Code;
To request the Court for settlement
Article 189. Settlement of individual labor disputes by the Labor Arbitration Council

On the basis of mutual agreement, the disputing parties may request dispute settlement by a Labor Arbitration Council in cases as prescribed in Clause 7, Article 188 of this Code. When the parties have requested the Labor Arbitration Council to resolve the dispute, they are not allowed to request for dispute settlement by the Court during the duration that the Labor Arbitration Council is resolving the dispute, except for the cases specified in Clause 4 of this Article
Within 07 working days after receiving the request for dispute settlement as specified in Clause 1 of this Article, an Arbitration panel shall be established for dispute settlement
Within 30 working days after the Arbitration Panel is established, this panel must issue a judgement on the dispute settlement and send this judgement to the disputing parties

In case where the Arbitration Panel is not established within the time limit as prescribed in Clause 2 of this Article or the Arbitration Panel fails to resolve the dispute within the time limit as prescribed at Clause 3 of this Article, the parties shall have the right to request for the dispute settlement by the People’s Court

In case where one of the disputing parties does not comply with the judgement on the dispute settlement of the Arbitration Panel, other parties have the right to request for the dispute settlement by the Court
Article 190. Time limit for requesting the settlement of individual labor disputes

The time limit to request a labor conciliator to settle an individual labor dispute is 06 months from the date on which the act, which a party claims has caused the infringement of the lawful rights or interests, is detected

The time limit to request the settlement of an individual dispute by the Labor Arbitration Council is 09 months from the date on which the act, which a party claims has caused the infringement of the lawful rights or interests, is detected

The time limit to bring an individual labor dispute to the People’s Court is 01 year from the date on which the act, which a party claims has caused the infringement of the lawful rights or interests, is detected

In case the requesting party can prove that due to a force majeure event, an objective obstacle or other reason prescribed by law it cannot request the settlement of an individual labor dispute within the time limit as prescribed in this Article, the time of the force majeure event or the objective obstacle or the reason shall not be included in the statute of limitations for requesting the settlement of the individual labor dispute
SECTION 3
COMPETENCE AND PROCEDURES FOR THE SETTLEMENT OF RIGHT-BASED COLLECTIVE LABOR DISPUTES
Article 191. Competence for the settlement of right-based collective labor disputes
Agencies, organizations and individuals who are competent to settle right-based collective labor disputes shall include
The Labor conciliator;
The Labor Arbitration Council;
The People’s Court
Right-based collective labor disputes must be settled through conciliation procedures of labor conciliators before requesting for the settlement by the Labor Arbitration Council or the People’s Court
Article 192. Procedures and formalities for the settlement of right-based collective labor disputes
Procedures and formalities for the settlement of right-based collective labor disputes shall be implemented under regulations in Clauses 2, 3, 4, 5 and 6 of Article 188 of this Code;

In case of unsuccessful conciliation or in case where the labor conciliator fails to conduct conciliation within the time limit as specified in Clause 2, Article 188 of this Code, the disputing parties shall have the right to choose one of the following methods to settle labor disputes
To request the Labor Arbitration Council for settlement as prescribed in Article 193 of this Code;
To request the Court for settlement
Article 193. Settlement of right-based collective labor disputes by the Labor Arbitration Council

In case of unsuccessful conciliation; in case where the labor conciliator fails to resolve the disputes within the time limits as prescribed in Clause 2, Article 188 of this Code; or in case where either party does not implement the agreement written in the record of successful conciliation - the disputing parties, on the basis of mutual agreement, may request the dispute settlement by a Labor Arbitration Council
Within 07 working days after receiving the request for dispute settlement as specified in Clause 1 of this Article, an Arbitration Panel shall be established for settling disputes

Within 30 working days after the Arbitration Panel is established, on the basis of provisions of labor law, collective bargaining agreements and registered internal work rules and other lawful agreements and regulations, this Panel must issue a judgement on the dispute settlement and send this judgement to the disputing parties

In case the disputing parties choose to have the Labor Arbitration Council settle their disputes under regulations of this Article, during the process of dispute settlement by the Labor Arbitration Council, the disputing parties must not request for the settlement of the People’s Court

In case where an Arbitration Panel is not established within the time limit as prescribed in Clause 2 of this Article or the Arbitration Panel fails to resolve the dispute within the time limit as prescribed at Clause 3 of this Article, the parties shall have the right to request for the dispute settlement by the Court

In case where one of the disputing parties does not comply with the judgement on the dispute settlement of the Arbitration Panel, other parties have the right to request for the dispute settlement by the People’s Court
Article 194. Time limit for the settlement of right-based collective labor disputes

The time limit to request a labor conciliator to settle a right-based collective labor dispute is 06 months from the date on which the act, which a party claims has caused the infringement of the lawful rights or interests, is detected

The time limit to request the settlement of a right-based collective labor dispute by the Labor Arbitration Council is 09 months from the date on which the act, which a party claims has caused the infringement of the lawful rights or interests, is detected

The time limit to bring a right-based collective labor dispute to the People’s Court is 01 year from the date on which the act, which a party claims has caused the infringement of the lawful rights or interests, is detected
SECTION 4
COMPETENCE AND PROCEDURES FOR THE SETTLEMENT OF RIGHT-BASED LABOR DISPUTES
Article 195. Competence for the settlement of interest-based collective labor disputes
Agencies, organizations and individuals who are competent to settle interest-based collective labor disputes shall include
The Labor conciliator;
The Labor Arbitration Council;

Interest-based collective labor disputes must be settled through conciliation procedures of labor conciliators before requesting for the settlement by the Labor Arbitration Council or carrying out procedures for going on strike
Article 196. Procedures and formalities for the settlement of right-based collective labor disputes
Procedures and formalities for the settlement of right-based collective labor disputes shall comply with regulations in Clauses 2, 3, 4 and 5, Article 188 of this Code;

In case of successful conciliation, the record of successful conciliation shall include all contents agreed upon by all disputing parties, and signatures of those parties and the labor conciliator. The record of successful conciliation shall be considered as a legal document of the enterprise’s collective bargaining agreement

In case of unsuccessful conciliation, in case where the labor conciliator fails to resolve the disputes within the time limits as prescribed in Clause 2, Article 188 of this Code; or in case where either party does not implement the agreement written in the record of successful conciliation, the disputing parties have the right to choose one of the following methods to settle their labor disputes
To request the Arbitration Council for settlement as prescribed in Article 197 of this Code;
Worker’s representative organizations have the right to conduct procedures for going on a strike as prescribed in Articles 200, 201, and 202 of this Code
Article 197. Settlement of interest-based collective labor disputes by the Labor Arbitration Council

In case of unsuccessful conciliation; in case where the labor conciliator fails to resolve the disputes within the time limits as prescribed in Clause 2, Article 188 of this Code; or in case where either party does not implement the agreement written in the record of successful conciliation - the disputing parties, on the basis of mutual agreement, may request the dispute settlement by a Labor Arbitration Council
Within 07 working days after receiving the request for dispute settlement as specified in Clause 1 of this Article, an Arbitration Panel shall be established for dispute settlement

Within 30 working days after the Arbitration panel is established, on the basis of provisions of labor law, collective bargaining agreements and registered internal work rules and other lawful agreements and regulations, this panel must issue a judgement on the dispute settlement and send this judgement to the disputing parties

In case the disputing parties choose to have the Labor Arbitration Council settle their disputes under regulations of this Article, during the process of dispute settlement by the Labor Arbitration Council, the disputing parties must not carry out a strike
SECTION 5
STRIKE
Article 198. Strike

Strike is a temporary, voluntary and organized work stoppage of an employees’ collective in order to achieve their demands in the process of labor dispute settlement. Strikes are organized and led by the workers’ representative organization, who has the right to conduct collective bargaining, as a disputing party
Article 199. Cases where employees shall have the right to strike
In case of unsuccessful conciliation or in case where the labor conciliator fails to resolve the disputes within the time limits as prescribed in Clause 2, Article 188 of this Code;

In case where a Labor Arbitration Panel is not established within the time limit; in case where the Labor Arbitration Panel is established but this Panel fails to resolve the dispute; or in case the employer as a disputing party does not conform to the judgement of the Labor Arbitration Panel
Article 200. Sequence of going on strike
Collecting opinions on the strike as prescribed in Article 201 of this Code;
Issuing a decision to go on strike and a notice of strike as prescribed in Article 202 of this Code;
Going on strike
Article 201. Collecting opinions on the strike

Before commencing a strike, the workers’ representative organization which has the right to organize and lead a strike as prescribed in Article 198 of this Code shall take the responsibility for collecting opinions of all employees or members of the Board of leaders of the workers’ representative organization participating in the negotiation
Issues to be put up for opinions on going on a strike include
Approval or disapproval of the strike;
The option suggested by the workers’ representative organization on the contents specified at Points b, c and d, Clause 2, Article 202 of this Code;
Opinions may be collected by ballot or signatures or other prescribed methods

The time, venue and method of collecting opinions on going on a strike must be determined by the workers’ representative organization and must be notified to the employer at least 01 day in advance. The solicitation of opinion must not leave adverse impacts on the normal business and manufacturing operation of the employer. The employer must not create any obstructions, difficulties or intervention in the solicitation of opinions on the strike conducted by the workers’ representative organization
Article 202. Decision of going on a strike and notification of the starting time of a strike

When over 50% of the consulted employees agree with the matters of strike putting forward for opinions as prescribed in Clause 2, Article 201 of this Code, the workers’ representative organization shall issue a written decision to go on strike
A decision to go on strike must include
The outcome of the collection of opinions on going on strike;
The starting time and venue for the strike;
Scope of the strike;
Demands of the employees;
Full name and address of the representative of the workers’ representative organization organizing and leading the strike

At least 05 working days prior to the starting date of the strike, the workers’ representative organization organizing and leading the strike shall send the decision to go on strike to the employer, district-level People’s Committee and the competent agency on labor under provincial People’s Committee
By the starting time of the strike, if the employer does not accept the demands of the employees, the workers’ representative organization may organize and lead the strike
Article 203. Rights of the parties prior to and during a strike
To continue negotiating to settle the collective labor dispute or jointly request a labor conciliator or the Labor Arbitration Council to settle labor disputes
The workers’ representative organization organizing and leading a strike as prescribed in Article 198 of this Code shall have the following rights
To withdraw the decision to go on strike if the strike has not happened yet or to stop the strike if it is happening;
To request the Court to declare the strike is legal
The employer shall have the following rights
To accept the demand entirely or in parts, and send a written notice of his/her acceptance to the workers’ representative organization that organizes and leads the strike;
To temporarily close the workplace during the strike due to shortage of conditions to maintain normal operations or to protect the assets;
To request the Court to declare the strike is illegal
Article 204. Cases in which a strike is illegal
The strike does not fall into any cases prescribed in Article 199 of this Code
The strike is not organized and led by a workers’ representative organization which have the right to organize and lead a strike
The strike violates regulations on procedures and formalities to go on strikes in accordance with this Code;
When the labor dispute is being settled by competent agencies, organizations and individuals under provisions of this Code;
The strike is conducted in case where a strike is prohibited as prescribed in Article 209 of this Code;
The strike occurs when the decision to postpone or cancel the strike has been issued by competent agencies in accordance with provisions in Article 210 of this Code;
Article 205. Notice of the decision on temporary closure of the workplace
The workers’ representative organization that is organizing and leading the strike;
The provincial-level People’s Committee of the locality where the workplace is located;
The district-level People’s Committee of the locality where the work place is located
Article 206. Prohibited cases of temporary closure of the workplace
12 hours prior to the starting time of the strike notified in the decision to go on strike
After the employees stop striking
Article 207. Wages and other lawful interests of employees during a strike

Employees who do not take part in a strike but have to stop working because of the strike shall be paid with a work suspension allowance under Clause 2, Article 99 of this Code and other benefits prescribed in the labor law
Employees taking part in a strike may not be paid with wages or other benefits as prescribed by the law, unless otherwise agreed by both parties
Article 208. Prohibited acts before, during and after a strike
Obstructing employees to exercise their rights to go on strike or instigating, dragging or forcing employees to go on strike, and preventing non-strikers from going to work
Using violence; sabotaging machines, equipment and assets of the employer
Violating public order and security

Terminating the labor contracts with, or imposing labor disciplinary measures on employees and strike leaders or transferring employees and strike leaders to other jobs or other locations due to their preparation for or their involvement in the strike
Taking revenge actions on employees who are on strike or leaders of the strike
Taking advantage of the strike to commit other illegal acts
Article 209. Workplaces where strikes are prohibited
Strike is prohibited in working places where strikes can threaten the national defense, public security, social order and human health

The Government shall detail the list of workplaces where strikes are prohibited and the settlement of labor disputes in workplaces where strikes are prohibited as specified in Clause 1 of this Article
Article 210. Decisions to postpone or cancel strikes

When considering that a strike may cause serious damage to the national economy and public interests or may threaten national defense, public security, social order and human health, the Chairperson of the provincial-level People’s Committee shall decide to postpone or cancel such strike
The Government shall detail regulations on the postponement and cancellation of strikes and the settlement of interests of the employees
Article 211. Handling of strikes that do not follow the prescribed sequence and procedures
CHAPTER XV
STATE MANAGEMENT OF LABOR
Article 212. Contents of state management of labor
Promulgating and implementing legal documents on labor

Monitoring, making statistics and providing information on labor supply and demand and fluctuations of labor supply and demand; making decision on policies, master plans and plans on human resources, distribution and utilization of labor in the whole society, vocational training, development of vocational skills; formulating the national vocational qualification framework and the national qualification framework for levels of vocational training. Issuing a list of jobs that require employees who have been vocationally trained or possess national vocational skills certificates;

Organizing and conducting scientific research on labor; collecting statistics and information on labor and the labor market and on the living standards, wages and income level of employees; managing the labor quality, quantity and labor fluctuation
